    The app now says that the pass opens the supporter drops but not the limited ones, that the monthly Sparks do not carry over, and that a refund can leave your balance below zero until your next pack. After you pay for a pack, the app now tells you what really happens: if it can match your payment the Sparks arrive by themselves, otherwise it asks you to check your email for the code. Bit can explain the 7-day trial and what a trial, a supporter, a Sparks buyer and a former supporter each get.

  • The Xenon menu holds what you use right now

    The Capture section now has only what you pick at that moment: what a recording takes (PC sound, microphone or none, and the corner of your webcam), Instant Replay on or off and how much it keeps. Quality, frame rate, folders, space and automatic clips, which you set once, stay in Settings, and the last row takes you there. Record says on its tile when it will take your microphone or webcam, so you know before you press. A key you make for Record from the menu follows the same choice. Game companion and Do not disturb are now in the menu too. A widget can still never turn on your microphone or webcam.

  • Who sells and how to get your money back, written where you buy

    Under the packs, the Sparks tab says that Xenon is the seller, that you pay on Buy Me a Coffee, and that within 14 days you can get a pack refunded by writing to the address shown. A refund removes the pack and what you bought with those Sparks. The FAQ says the same for membership payments, and Bit can answer it too.

  • The Windows app opens sooner after you sign in

    Windows starts the programs in its startup list one at a time and can wait half a minute for each, so Xenon often came up a minute or more late. It now starts by itself a few seconds after sign-in. The startup list entry stays as a fallback.

  • Saving is much lighter with picture scenes

    The pictures of your Ambient scenes now live in files of their own instead of inside the settings file, so changing a single switch no longer saves and sends megabytes of pictures to every open screen. In a test with one photo scene the settings file went from about 1.3 MB to 17 KB. Backups and shared scenes still carry the pictures inside, so nothing changes when you move to another PC or share a scene.

  • Bit costs fewer Sparks per message

    Bit now keeps the tools you need less often (screen capture and recording, game performance, widgets on the PC screen, desktop settings, lighting effects, making a widget or a theme) to one side and picks them up the moment you ask for one of those things. Each message sends much less, so it costs less, and nothing Bit can do went away.

  • Every Deck action says what it does, and sits where you would look for it

    In the action list of a Deck key, tap the (i) next to an action to read what it does without picking it; the action you chose shows the same line under it. The explanations are in every language of the app, and the search finds words from them too ("liked songs" finds the Spotify save). The categories are clearer: Apps and websites (open an app, a file, a page, a Steam game, a script or a webhook), System (shortcuts, typing, lock, move a window, power mode, do not disturb), Phone (call and text) and Xenon (dashboard pages, Deck states, the Xenon menu, the widgets on your screen, the animated wallpaper), so the old mixed Windows group is gone. Your keys keep working as they are. Bit reads the same explanations when it builds a Deck for you.

  • Game Companion works with the AI you chose for Bit

    It used to need a Gemini key even when Bit ran on Sparks or on your own ChatGPT or Claude key. Now it looks at your game with whatever Bit uses: Sparks, your key, or an Ollama model that can see pictures. If that AI cannot look at a screen (Claude Code, Codex, an Ollama model without vision), the card says so before taking any screenshot. On Sparks, a small line under the buttons says what one look costs before you press, and after a look it shows what that one cost. When your Sparks run out, the card says that too, with a link to recharge. Its answers now also come in Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Russian and Dutch, not in English.

  • Bit's chat is easier to start and calmer to read

    An empty chat now greets you for the time of day and offers three things to ask that fit your PC: the weather in the city you set, a timer (that also turns the music down when something is playing) and a widget, with its rough price on Sparks. On a short tile the empty chat never scrolls: it leaves out the big Bit, then the line, the hello and the last suggestions, until what is left fits. The head shows your Sparks balance; a tap opens Top up and the model that makes widgets, now called Fast, Smart and Smartest, with what a widget costs on each. The composer has one green button: it dictates while the field is empty, sends once you have written something and stops a reply on its way; the full voice conversation stays on Bit in the top bar. Under a reply, suggestions are quiet lines instead of a row of buttons, and after Bit changes something it offers at most two next steps. Undo is plain underlined text that also works in a copy of the chat and tells you when it fails, and a reply that fails keeps your question with Try again now. Without Sparks or a key, the chat says what it needs: Get Sparks, or use your own Gemini key. On a phone, a tap on the chat opens it full screen, and the arrow, Escape or the phone's back button bring the dashboard back.

  • What the AI assistant makes stays light on your PC

    Before you see an animated background or a widget that draws on a canvas, the assistant now checks what its code does on every frame: reading or rewriting every pixel, blurring the whole picture, creating new images or arrays each time. It rewrites what would cost the whole screen 30 times a second (for example a blur done once instead of on every frame) and weighs the rest. The Store review runs the same checks on what creators send.

  • An animated background that weighs on your PC now lightens itself

    Xenon now times every frame an animated background draws. If one keeps using too much of the processor, it first draws half as many frames, then at a lower resolution, and as a last step stays still as a picture, with a note saying so. Light backgrounds are never touched. You can turn this off in Settings, Background, with "Lighten heavy backgrounds".

  • Every way to support Xenon now says it comes with 300 Sparks a month

    The plans in Settings → Support Xenon, the Supporters panel in the Store, Bit's message about supporting Xenon, the December note and the end of the 7-day trial all name the Sparks, Xenon's credits, with their spark beside them. Every plan brings them, the one-time ones too for the months they cover.

  • Sparks now have their own tab in the Store

    It shows your balance, the three packs (500 Sparks for 5 USD, 1,050 for 10 USD, 2,200 for 20 USD) and what Sparks are for: making widgets, themes and pages with Bit, building with Bit in Xenon Maker, and unlocking Store items sold for Sparks, which are listed right there. Each pack says about how many widgets it makes with each model (Haiku, Sonnet and Opus), the pack that gives the most Sparks per dollar is marked, and the tab says which email to pay with and tells you when the Sparks arrive. It also shows the supporter plan as one card: 5 USD a month, 300 Sparks every month, a new supporter pack every month and what you unlock stays yours, with a button to join; if this PC keeps a supporter code, the card says it is included and shows no button to join. The Sparks balance now stays in view in Settings and in the Store whatever assistant you use. The Store page on the website does the same: the plan card once on the page, the Sparks section with the packs and what each makes, and no pack shown twice. Every "Buy Sparks" in the app leads to this tab: the Sparks button in Settings, the balance chip, Bit's chat when your Sparks run low or out (once, under the reply that crosses the mark, and under a request refused for an empty balance), Bit's monthly letter about a low balance, and the unlock window. You can also ask Bit to open it. In Settings the Sparks rows say what your balance makes and when the Sparks included with your support come back.

  • News from Xenon comes from Bit, and nothing pops up over what you are doing

    New supporter creations and limited editions, announcements, polls, low Sparks, the one-time invitation to share your setup and the one-time supporter ask all arrive the same way: a small card with Bit at the top centre of the dashboard and of "widgets only", at the bottom on a phone. It waits until you read it, shows at most one new message a day, and stays away while you are typing, talking to Bit, playing, on the lock screen or in an Ambient scene. Open it to see the picture and the text in place, and answer a poll with one tap. A big announcement can fill the screen instead; in "widgets only" it starts as the small card and opens when you ask. Read it on one screen and it is gone from the others. Afterwards it stays in the chat with Bit as something Bit said, with its picture and its button, so you can reply to it. Ask Bit to open a creation it told you about, or to turn the news or the month's creations off. The December corner card is unchanged.

  • The dots on the top bar buttons stay visible on narrow screens

    When the buttons shrink to icons, on a phone or a small window, the dot that says an update is waiting used to disappear with the labels. It now stays on the icon.

  • You can see when Performance Mode is on, and turn it off with one tap

    While Performance Mode runs it can pause animations, the animated background, the Media wave and heavy tiles, and until now only the System tile showed it, so many people thought Xenon was broken. Now a Performance button sits next to the clock in the top bar while it is on, in every top bar style, and one tap turns it off and puts everything back. In Settings → Performance, Button always in the top bar keeps it there all the time, so you can also turn Performance Mode on whenever you want. You can hide it like the other items in Settings → Top bar.

  • Neater notifications

    The icon, the first lines of text and the close button now line up on every notification, a short one is centred on its icon, and a title gets two lines before it is cut. The glass is a little denser, so a bright tile behind a notification no longer shows through in colour, most of all on a light theme. Notifications arrive with a gentle spring, the ones below glide to make room on the same spring, and a success draws its tick as it appears. With the minimal top bar, the notification island no longer shows its text outside the glass while it opens or closes, moves straight from one notification to the next, and keeps the "+N" counter beside the close button instead of on an empty second line. With reduced motion turned on in your system, they simply fade in and out.

  • Finding an action for a Deck key is quicker

    The action list in a key's What it does tab now opens as a short list of categories, each with its icon and how many actions it holds; tap one to open it, and the category of the key's current action starts open. Every action has its own icon, also on the closed list, so you see what a key does at a glance. A search box at the top finds an action by any word of its name, in any order, without caring about accents or capitals, and also by its English name or its category ("spotify", "cattura", "screenshot"); the words you typed are highlighted and the arrow keys and Enter pick a result without the mouse. Your last five actions sit at the top under Recently used. Services that still need setting up (OBS, Discord, Home Assistant and the others) move to the end of the list and say where to set them up. On a phone or touch screen the keyboard does not pop up by itself.

  • New good morning, afternoon and evening screens

    The daily greeting is now a pixel landscape of the hour (sunrise, clouds, sunset, a night with a moon and stars) with Bit in it: having coffee in the morning, in sunglasses in the afternoon, reading in the evening, asleep at night. The line under the greeting is now something true about your day, such as "3 events today, the first at 9:30" or "Next event at 18:30", instead of a generic pleasantry, and it is left out when your calendar has nothing to say. It fits any screen, phone included.

  • A new logo: Bit next to the name

    The app icon, the site, the favicon, the emails and the README now show Bit, Xenon's pixel guardian, beside the word "xenon". The icons are drawn pixel by pixel at every size, so Bit stays sharp on the taskbar and in the tray, and phone notifications get a clean white badge.

  • One calmer look, where colour means something

    The site, the app icon, the setup screen and Settings now share the same neutral greys. Colour is kept for Bit's moods: green when all is well, orange for a warning, red for a problem, so a coloured thing is always telling you something. On the site, in Xenon Maker, in the emails and on the setup screen, the main button, such as Download or Support, is filled with Bit's green, the colour of the logo, so it is the first thing you find; everything else stays grey. The "Beta" tags are small outlined labels, so they no longer look like buttons. In the site catalog, supporter and limited items are named in words instead of gold and purple. The grey text under titles is a little brighter, so it is easier to read on every surface. The app now uses the same typeface as the site and Xenon Maker, Sofia Sans, sized so every tile, button and menu keeps the exact place and line height it had; Russian and Greek are included, and a font you chose yourself stays as it is.

  • Say "Hey Bit" to start a voice chat

    The wake word is now "Hey Bit", the name of the assistant, in every language and in Settings. The "Hey" is needed, because "bit" alone is an everyday word, so saying "a bit" or "bit by bit" never opens the chat. "Hey Xenon" still works too.

  • The AI provider in Settings is called Bit

    The provider chip that read "Scintille" now says Bit, in every language. Scintille stay the name of the credits.

  • The AI chat has a face: Bit

    The chat tile now shows Bit, Xenon's little pixel guardian, at the top. It thinks while the AI works, nods when an answer did something for you, looks worried after an error, and greets you in a way that fits the time of day. A small Bit sits beside each reply. While a long answer is on its way, the chat lists the steps it went through, each ticked off when the next one starts. An answer paid with Sparks shows under it what it cost and how much is left. The paperclip now opens a small menu: attach a file, or send the screen with every message (this replaces the separate screen button). A new button next to Send starts a voice conversation, and New chat moved to the top of the tile. While Bit answers, Send turns into a square stop button: the reply ends before its next step, a step already under way still finishes (and is paid, if it runs on Sparks), and anything it already did for you stays done. With the light theme the chat is now light too, instead of a dark block. Voice conversations show Bit too, in place of the glowing ring: it listens, thinks and talks, with small bars under it while someone speaks. On a wide screen like the Xeneon Edge, Bit stands on the left and the words appear beside it. With the see-through voice option, everything sits in one card at the bottom: a small Bit, what it heard, its answer, and whether it is listening, thinking or talking. Bit stands still when animations are paused, in a game, behind an open overlay and with reduced motion. Bit is also on the AI button in the top bar (and in the phone's bottom bar), drawn in the button's own colour like the icons beside it so it reads on any accent, on the search bar's AI switch, where it thinks while it reads your phrase, on the Game Companion button while you play, and on the Deck's AI action. The search bar's close button is now centred in its circle. Tapping the Game Companion button opens Bit's card: Bit with the game's name, session time and FPS, and its answers beside a small Bit that looks at the screen while it reads it, smiles when it answers and looks worried when something goes wrong. The card follows your theme, light or dark.

  • A package now asks for its name

    Settings → Widgets & sharing → Export package has a Package name field at the top. It used to name every package "My Xenon package" without asking, and that name travelled with it into the Store. The field turns red if you press Create package while it is empty.

  • A package can now carry your wallpaper picture

    Export package has a new Wallpaper picture row, ticked by default and easy to untick. Before, the picture stayed behind without a word, so people who installed a package got the colours but not the photo. Large photos are shrunk to about 2 MB so the package still imports. Video wallpapers are not included. Uninstalling the package removes its picture, and leaves alone any wallpaper you set afterwards.

  • Shared Deck keys no longer carry your personal details

    A Deck profile you share, alone or in a package, now leaves out the app and file paths, phone numbers, webhook addresses, alarm codes, Discord users, Claude projects and audio, Spotify, Wave Link and lighting device choices. Before, a key that opened C:\Users\<your name>\... sent that path to everyone, and it pointed nowhere on their PC. The keys keep their icon, name and action. Whoever imports them sees how many need their own app, file or device. Pressing one that is still empty tells you to set it up in the Deck editor, where before it gave a path error. When you export, Xenon tells you how many keys will need setting up.

  • Importing a supporter item is tidier

    If a supporter code is saved on this PC, the import window now says one line, that your code unlocks it, and Import does the rest. Before, it also offered the 7-day free trial to people who already had a code. The trial offer now shows only when there is no code and no trial on this PC. From the Store, the window shows the item's name instead of a box full of code. To forget a saved code, use Settings, as before.

  • No more dead end without a code

    If you open a supporter item without a code, and the free trial is used or does not cover it, the unlock window now tells you how to get one, with a Become a supporter button. If a code is saved on this PC, none of this shows. Items installed from the Store also no longer ask you to keep a code: the Store installs them again for you.

  • The Store's buttons are easier to reach

    On a phone, an item's Become a supporter and Unlock buttons stay at the bottom of the screen while you read its description.

  • Cleaner text

    The app's text no longer uses long dashes, in every language.

  • Less memory with the animated background off

    When the aurora, grid or a custom background is switched off (also in game mode and performance mode), the dashboard no longer keeps it drawn out of sight. In our tests on a screen driven by built-in graphics, where video memory is shared with the PC's RAM, this saved about 120 MB. The look and the fade in and out are unchanged.

  • Less memory while Xenon is hidden (Windows app)

    When the dashboard window is hidden (dashboard on your phone, Widgets only, hidden from the tray, during Remote Desktop), while the search window is closed and while widgets on the screen are hidden behind a full-screen app, Xenon now asks Windows to take back the memory it is not using. Everything keeps running: widgets, alerts and updates work as before. In our tests a hidden dashboard went from about 1.5 GB of RAM to between 0.1 and 0.65 GB, and it takes the memory back by itself when you show it again.

  • Widgets made by the AI assistant land on your page in the right shape

    When the assistant makes a widget, it now puts it on the page you are looking at, in the shape it was drawn for (a wide strip, a tall column, a small square), measured on your screen, instead of a default box squeezed into any free corner. If a smaller hole is free, the tile shrinks as a whole and keeps its proportions; if the page has no room for it, the widget gets a page of its own, named after it, instead of squeezing the tiles already there. A widget is placed once, even when the assistant corrects it before answering, and a new version of a widget already on a tile only refreshes that tile. The assistant also checks each widget it makes, the same way the Store review does, and fixes what it finds before telling you it is done. It also checks that the widget still fits when its tile changes shape (wider, taller, or on a phone), so text and pictures no longer spill out of a tile that is a different size from the one it was drawn for.

  • Widget makers can say which shape their widget wants

    A widget's manifest can name a size (small, medium, wide, tall or large), and a new tile of it starts in that shape on any screen. On the phone view tiles keep their usual stacking. See the Widget SDK guide.

  • Settings → Bit is easier to read

    The long guide at the top is gone. The page starts with Sparks, then who answers: eight keys in one grid, one for each assistant, and the model right under them, with Download model beside the model it downloads. Each option has one short line that says what it does. Live voice is shown only with Gemini, the one assistant that runs it, and the advanced features now say plainly that they spend Sparks or quota even when you are not typing. Claude Code, Codex and a local server show their state as plain rows with Check again on the right, and How to install goes away once the program is ready.

  • Installing from the Store goes straight to what you are adding

    A code that arrives whole, from the Store, a link or the AI assistant, now opens directly on the list of what it contains, without the step where you paste it. Protected drops still ask for their code first, and items with a performance note still show the note before you go on.

  • Creators can follow the review of what they send to the Store

    After sending a creation from the website, you get a private link. It shows where the review stands, the reviewer's note, and a report that lists what to fix, where, why and how, with the quickest fixes first and an estimate of the time each takes. Keep the link: it is the only copy.

  • Supporters' creations are reviewed first

    The website's submit form has an optional field for your supporter code. The code is checked when you send and never stored.

  • The check on the submit form and your status page says first what it adds up to

    Above the findings, one line in your language says how many must be fixed and how many only need a look. The findings follow in groups, heaviest first, each with a red or orange bar beside it, so what holds a submission back is the first thing you see.

  • Design suggestions when you submit a creation

    The website's submit form now lists design tips next to the automatic check: low contrast, text too small, colours that ignore the dashboard theme, and looks that read as made by an AI. Each tip says how to fix it. They never block a submission.

  • A suggested price on your review report

    The website's submit form has an optional field for the price you would ask, in USD. The report shows it next to a suggested price from free to 10 USD. It starts from what your creation contains, goes up a step for a clean check or down for one with many points to fix, and up a step when similar entries in the Store are installed a lot and well rated. The report says why, and lists those similar entries with their installs and stars. You choose the price; the suggestion only explains a starting point.

  • Store descriptions can have paragraphs, lists and bold

    Creators can write the description of what they publish with simple Markdown: blank lines for paragraphs, lines starting with "-" or "1." for lists, \*\*bold\*\*, \*italic\* and \code\. The item page in the Store and on the website shows it formatted, the cards show the first lines as plain text, and a description can now be up to 800 characters instead of 300. Descriptions without Markdown look the same as before.

  • A clearer Support page in Settings

    The three ways to support are tiles you tap whole: 5 USD a month, 50 USD a year (with a theme made for you), or 5 or 25 USD once, each saying what it brings. Under them, people who already support can enter their code or import a pack file. Discord, GitHub and bug reports moved to the new About page. The old text about Buy Me a Coffee posts is gone, since perks now unlock with your supporter code.

  • The Lighting settings, rebuilt to match the rest of Settings

    The page was one long list. It now has four tabs: Devices (one card per light with what it shows: follows Xenon, a colour, an effect or off, and its parts), Effects (the manual colour and animations), Reactions (temperature, album colours and event flashes) and Connections (iCUE, Razer Chroma, network lights and SignalRGB). Every block uses the same cards, switches and buttons as the other Settings pages, the colour and effect controls appear only after you pick something, and the tab you were on is remembered.

  • Picking a colour for a Deck lighting action takes one tap

    Lighting actions on the Deck (a colour for the lights, a device or one part) show the same row of colours as the key's own look, with the full picker behind the last swatch, instead of the system colour window.

  • What a Deck key sets on the lights stays on screen

    A colour, an effect or one part set from a key now wins over the music and CPU temperature colours until you switch the lights off from a key, so a key that darkens everything and lights one strip does exactly that. Colouring one part from a key no longer changes the map you saved in Lighting.

  • A Lights on/off key on the Deck shows whether the lights are on

    A key that turns the lights on and off now follows the lights themselves: it wears its On look while they are on, and changes when you switch them from Settings, the Lighting tile, another screen or another key, not only when you tap it. Before, a plain key with that action never changed its look. Keys you already have pick this up the next time you open them in the editor and save.

  • Ambient settings are easier to read

    Settings → Ambient is now three blocks: when it opens (on, at startup, after how long idle), which scene it shows, and your scenes. The choice of what the Classic scene shows (clock, weather, music, events) sits right under the scene picker and appears only while the Classic scene is picked. The Delete button on each of your scenes shows its label again (it was red text on red), and the scene in use says so. My scenes now shows the three ways to get a scene: Create in Xenon Maker, Import code and Gallery. Scenes installed from the gallery are listed there too, with a note that they are picked as they are and cannot be edited.

  • The key editor is easier to follow

    It has four tabs, in the order you set a key up: What it does (type, gesture, action), State (when the key lights up: as a switch, or following a widget or script, plus the live value it shows), Look and Effects (tap effect and its colour, animation, LED reaction, and the ring, dimming and motion while the key is on). Look edits one face at a time: pick Off or On at the top, or tap either key in the preview. On shows only what can change while lit: label text and colour, icon and icon colour, background colour or gradient. Anything left empty looks the same as off, so a key that reads OFF and turns to ON in green is two fields. If the key never lights up, On says so and offers Make it a switch, which turns it into a key that each tap lights up or turns off, or Open State to choose what lights it. Trigger is now called Gesture.

  • The Deck key editor shows a key on and off side by side

    What changes when a key is active now has its own tab, On. At the top, one line says what lights the key (the mic, a switch, a scene...) or that nothing does yet. The preview shows the key twice, off and on, so you see the difference while you set it. The lit face can now also change the icon colour, the text colour and add a second colour for a gradient, draw a ring, play a motion while on (Pulse, Breathe or Blink, which stop in power saving and with reduced motion), and dim the key while it is off.

  • Deck appearance is easier to read

    The window is split into Keys, Lit keys, Background and Music. Colour and gradient choices use switches, and their colour pickers appear only when the option is on. The remove button next to an image no longer shows when there is no image.

  • Widgets can show the frame rate of your game

    A widget from the Store or one you make can ask for the new perf permission and get what the Game performance tile shows: FPS, 1% and 0.1% low, the latest frame times for a graph, and your last game when nothing runs. Readings arrive only while a game runs; otherwise the stream sends nothing. Windows reads every number; on Linux only the FPS; on macOS none, because the system does not let an app read another app's frames. The SDK guide has a new section on it.

  • Widgets can show the games you played

    With the new gameSessions permission a widget reads the list from Settings → Performance → Games played: each game with its average FPS, lows, load and highest temperatures, and how the latest one compares with the time before. Nothing is read while "Games played" is off.

  • Widgets can show where your connection slows down

    With the new netPath permission a widget reads, about once a second, the delay and the lost packets from this PC to your router, to your provider and to the internet, with the Wi-Fi signal and how much this PC is downloading and uploading. It gets numbers only, never an address or the name of your network. The measuring starts when such a widget is on screen and stops 10 seconds after it is not. On Windows no program is started for it; on macOS and Linux it uses the system's ping and trace tools. The SDK guide has a new section on it.

  • A widget over a game can let your clicks through

    A widget on the desktop, over everything or beside an app can now ask for the mouse to go to whatever is under it while it stays on screen, so a counter in the corner of a game never catches a click meant for the game. It can take the clicks back when it needs them. When you edit your widgets they all take clicks again, so you can always move or remove them, and the tabs of a group always stay pressable. A widget that opens at full size on the desktop or over a game now fills that screen, and closes with its ✕. The SDK guide has a new section on it.

  • Widgets know where they are

    A widget is told whether it sits on the dashboard, on the desktop, over a game or next to another app's window, and whether you use Xenon with widgets only, so it can lay itself out for that place. It needs no permission and cannot move itself: where it goes is still your choice.

  • Widgets can start a benchmark, open the gallery and show or hide your screen widgets

    Each is its own permission you allow when you install the widget. A benchmark file stays on your PC and the widget never sees it; the gallery opens with your clips but the widget never gets the list; widgets can show, hide and switch pages of the widgets on your screen, but only you place and move them.

  • Fixed in the SDK example helper (xenon-client.js):

    a value that changed right as a widget started listening could be followed by the older one, leaving the widget on stale data.

  • Widgets can download bigger answers from the web

    A widget asking a website for data through Xenon could get at most 1 MB back, which a full sports scoreboard or a long feed can pass, so the request failed. The limit is now 4 MB. Pictures (map tiles and cached artwork) keep the 1 MB limit. The SDK guide also explains how to open a widget's developer console to debug it. Reported on Discord by SWu.

  • Tiles reopen on the tab you left them on

    Discord, Spotify, Streamer.bot, Twitch, YouTube, Phone, Football and Disk used to go back to their first tab after a reload or a restart. Each tile now remembers its own tab, so two Discord tiles can stay one on Notifications and one on Controls. Every screen keeps its own choice, so a paired phone does not change what the Edge shows. Suggested on Discord by SeibiRiho.

  • Play on the Spotify tile starts Spotify when it is closed

    Tapping Open Spotify and play opens the desktop app and starts the music on this computer, on Windows, macOS and Linux. On Windows and macOS a new setting under Spotify, Start Spotify minimized, keeps the app out of the way while it plays. If Spotify cannot start, or never shows up as a device, the tile says so. Suggested on Discord by SeibiRiho.

  • A smaller message box on the Claude tile, and pictures you can see

    The attach and send buttons now sit inside the text box (send is an arrow), so the box takes less room. An image you paste or attach shows as a preview before you send it, and images in the conversation (a screenshot Claude looked at, or one pasted in the terminal) appear in the thread, with a tap to open them full size. The thread also shows what Claude is doing between its sentences (the files it reads, the commands it runs), so plan mode no longer looks empty, and your own slash commands such as /plan show up as you typed them. A message you type in the terminal while Claude is still working now shows in the thread too. Long sessions with many screenshots no longer open as a blank thread. The header shows just the mascot.

  • Play, pause, previous and next on the Lyrics widget, with the album cover

    You can now control the song from the lyrics tile itself, and the cover sits next to the song name. On a narrow tile the cover is hidden first.

  • Lyrics translation spends nothing on songs already in your language

    Before asking your AI provider, Xenon now checks the lyrics on this PC. When they are clearly in your language, there is no request, nothing is counted against the monthly limit and no wait. Anything unclear (a mixed song, a short one, one with a line in another language, or one in a close language such as Catalan next to Spanish) is sent to the AI as before.

  • Lyrics translation with Sparks shows its cost in Sparks

    With Bit on Sparks, the Lyrics options say that translation runs on the smallest model and about how many Sparks it takes for a number of new songs, worked out from your own songs once there are some.

  • Change the model and the effort, or compact, from the top of a Claude Code session

    When a session is idle in a terminal that has the Xenon mod, the model and effort chips in the session header become menus and a Compact button appears. Each one runs the matching command (/model, /effort, /compact) in the session itself. They wait for the current turn to end. The permission mode stays a label: Claude Code has no command to change it. This needs the Xenon mod 0.4.0 for Claude Code; with an older mod the chips stay plain labels.

  • Start a Claude Code session in any folder

    The new-session screen only offered the few projects Claude Code already knew. A new "Another folder" button takes the full path of any folder on the PC; it is remembered and appears with the others from then on. Only from the PC itself, not from a paired phone.

  • /model, /effort and /plan work in a new session

    Typing them in the message box now sets the model, the effort or the plan mode of that run (/plan can be followed by what to plan), instead of sending them to Claude Code, which ignored them. They also appear in the "/" list.

  • A plan waiting for your approval shows in the side panel

    When Claude has written a plan and asks you to approve it, the side panel of the session opens on the Plan tab with the plan's text, next to the to-do steps. Model, effort and Compact changes also go through while Claude waits for that approval, instead of waiting for the end of the whole turn.

  • The plan is a roadmap on the right

    When Claude writes a plan, its phases appear in the Plan tab as a path: finished ones filled in, the one being worked lit, the rest waiting. It follows Claude's own task list when that has one entry per phase, and otherwise moves forward when Claude edits a file a phase names. The full plan stays one tap away, and it keeps showing after you approve it, even when the plan was written before Xenon started.

  • The "/" list in an open session is the terminal's own

    It shows every command and skill that session has, built-in ones like /plan, plugin skills and MCP prompts, each with its description, and picking one runs it in the session. Commands that would end the session (/exit, /quit, /logout, /login) are never offered. This needs the Xenon mod 0.5.0. After a command that takes a fixed choice, such as /model , /effort , /fast , /color , /mcp or /review , the box lists the values to pick from, as Claude Code does.

  • /model, /effort and /compact work while Claude is writing

    In a session that is busy, the "/" list and the model, effort and Compact buttons at the top are no longer locked: the command is held and runs by itself the moment the turn ends. Typing one in the message box now sends it too; before, any text starting with "/" was refused. It needs the Xenon mod 0.4.0 listening in that terminal: with an older mod the list and the buttons stay hidden, and a typed command is refused with a note to update the mod, instead of being sent to Claude as a message.

  • The "/" list now opens in a running Claude Code session too

    Type / in the message box of a session and you get the commands and skills with their descriptions, including /model, /effort and /compact, as in a new chat. Before, the list only appeared for new chats.

  • The side panel of a Claude Code session can be hidden, and it shows the plan

    A button at its top folds it away to give the conversation the full width, and a small button brings it back. When the session has a plan (its to-do list), two tabs, Activity and Plan, switch between the tool log and the plan: how many steps are done, a progress bar, and every step written in full.

  • The session status is part of the conversation

    The line that said "Ready for your next message" or what Claude is doing now used to sit in a bar above the chat. It is now the last line of the conversation, so the bar is gone and the chat has more room.

  • See what Claude changed in a file, like in the terminal

    In a session's tool log, each file edit now shows the file name with how many lines were added and removed. Tap it to open the lines: removed ones in red, added ones in green. Only the newest few edits keep their lines, and files that usually hold secrets (.env, keys, tokens) show the counts only.

  • The Claude and Codex icons in the clock island take you to their tile

    Tap the icon and the dashboard moves to the page that holds the Claude Code or Codex tile. For Claude, if a session has just finished, it opens too.

  • The Claude Code session list can fold to just the icons

    On a wide tile, a button above the list shrinks it to one Clawd per session, still in the session's colour and still moving the way the session is. Hover for the chat's name. Tap the button again to bring the full list back; the choice is remembered.

  • See what each Claude Code agent is doing

    When a session starts subagents, its side panel gets an Agents tab: each agent with what it was asked to do, the tool it is using and how long it has been running. Tap one to see its model, its effort, how many tools it has called, how full its context is and its last tool calls, and once it is done, its last answer. Finished agents stay in the list for two minutes. The "agents" chip at the top of the session opens the tab. With the Xenon mod 0.7.0 for Claude Code the figures arrive live; with an older mod they are read from the session's own files when you open an agent.

  • A hidden side panel still shows the essentials

    Folded away, the side panel of a Claude Code session becomes a slim strip. Each agent is a small Clawd in its own colour, walking while it works and asleep once it is done, with how long it has been running. The plan shows as one step per phase, filled as the work moves on, whether it is a written plan or a todo list. Tap the strip to open the panel again.

  • Calmer session icons in the Claude Code list

    Each session's Clawd now stands on its own in the session's colour, without a coloured square behind it, and is drawn at a sharp pixel size. The open session is marked by a plain background and a thin bar in its colour, instead of a ring and a tinted card. A session waiting for you turns amber and hops, with a square "!" next to it.

  • The Minimal clock island now cuts into the tile under it

    A tile that sits under the floating clock keeps its full size: the island takes a rounded bite out of its top edge, the tile's border follows the cut, and the content starts just below it. When the island grows or shrinks (a badge, a notification, a wider clock) the cut follows it with a short animation, or at once with reduced motion turned on in your system. A group of tabs the island only bites a corner of keeps its tabs at the top, beside the cut, and only what is under them moves down, so a wide island no longer leaves an empty band across the tiles next to it. Before, the tile moved its content down by the island's height, and sometimes the island covered the top of the tile instead.

  • Notifications open out of the Minimal clock island, one at a time

    In the Minimal top bar the clock island itself turns into the notification and back into the clock when it closes. It opens over your widgets without moving them. When more notifications arrive, the newest is shown and a "+2" next to it counts the others: tap it to see them all in a short list, open one or clear them all. When the shown one closes, the island turns straight into the next.

  • Notifications have a new, calmer look

    They use the same glass as the clock island, the app's icon sits in a solid coloured square, and the text is easier to read. The time left before a notification closes is now a thin ring around its close button, which stops while your finger or mouse is on it. Buttons and tappable notifications give a little under your finger.

  • Search finds a path you paste

    Paste a file or folder path into the search (as Explorer's "Copy as path" gives it, with or without quotes, or in the ~\Desktop\... form the results show) and that file or folder comes up, ready to open. If it is no longer there, the search looks for its name instead, so a file that was moved is still found. Works on Windows, macOS and Linux.

  • Supporters are no longer asked to become supporters

    If this PC keeps your supporter code, the new-drop card offers Unlock instead of "Become a supporter" and opens the unlock straight away, the Store's supporter panel shows your saved code instead of the membership offer, and during the Lyrics free week the tile offers to unlock with your code. If the code has ended, you are told so and the way to renew comes back.

  • More Home Assistant controls on Deck keys and in widgets

    The thermostat action can now pick Heat/Cool, set a range with two temperatures (type it as 20-24 in the Value field), set the humidity, and choose a fan mode, swing or preset by name. The media player action can turn the player on or off, pick a source or a sound mode by name, jump to a point in the track, and switch shuffle and repeat. A name must be one the device itself offers, so a typo does nothing instead of something unexpected. Widgets also get the cover of what is playing, the two setpoints of a Heat/Cool thermostat, and the speakers grouped with a player. The SDK guide is updated.

  • Put your Smart Home rooms and devices in the order you want

    Settings → Smart Home has a new list, Order on the tile, with up and down buttons for each room and for each device inside a room. A device you tick now goes to the end of its room instead of reshuffling the list. Before, rooms were always in alphabetical order. Asked on Discord by Forlin.

  • Smart Home devices made of sensors show their readings on the card

    A weather station or an air monitor shows up to three values on a card two columns wide (for example 820 ppm, 21.8° and 55%) instead of a count of its parts, so you see them without a tap. On a narrow tile, such as one on a phone, each card puts its icon and switch on top and the name below, so names are no longer cut short. A new option, Show devices, in Settings → Smart Home picks how the tile lays them out: Automatic (as before), Always open (every device's controls on the tile, which scrolls) or Compact (always cards).

  • Home Assistant widgets refresh only when your devices change

    Before, every change anywhere in Home Assistant (a power meter you never picked, ticking every second) refreshed the Smart Home tile and every Home Assistant widget. Now they refresh only when one of the devices you picked changes. A widget that asks for the history of a device you have since unticked still gets the rest of its charts.

  • A clearer Widget style editor

    Every control in Colors, Effects, Background and Decor now works from the first touch: no more tick box in front of each one that left the slider or the colour greyed out. A value still taken from the theme reads "Theme" next to it; once you change it, your value shows with a button to go back to the theme. Colours are grouped into Panel, Text, and Accent and states, and setting any colour, the gradient or the font makes the widget use your own colours, so the Follow theme / Customize switch is gone. A new option, Keep text readable, decides whether Xenon may adjust a text colour that would be hard to read, and the row says when it did. The background sliders appear once you pick a picture or a gradient. When the glass blur is on but the panel is solid, a button makes the panel see-through so the blur shows. The panel can be dragged by its title, and Copy style and Paste style carry the look of one widget to another.

  • Much more to choose in Widget style → Decor

    There are now 16 frames (dashed, dotted, stitched, corner brackets, HUD, pixel, Art Deco, circuit, vine, ornate and more) and 35 stickers sorted into Nature, Sky, Play, Cute, Paper, Seasons and Japan. A frame can take your colour or the theme's accent, a second colour, a glow, an inset from the edge and a slow pulse. Each sticker can be placed anywhere by dragging, resized, turned, flipped, recoloured, given a glow or a shadow, set to float, sway, spin, beat or twinkle, and put over the widget or behind it; a tile holds up to 8 stickers, which you can reorder and duplicate. New layers: a pattern behind or over the widget (dots, grid, lines, cross-hatch, checks, scan lines, zigzag or grain, with its colour, size, angle and a fade at the edges), an inner and outer glow, and a bar along one edge. Eleven ready-made looks (Neon HUD, Circuit board, Retro arcade, Gilded, Sakura dream, Cozy paper, Blueprint, Night sky, Garden, Spooky, Accent line) set all of this in one tap and keep your background picture. Moving decorations pause with the rest of the dashboard and follow the system's reduced motion setting.

  • Style the buttons inside a widget

    Widget style has a new tab, Controls, for the widget's own buttons, tabs and chips: pick a style (Filled, Soft, Outline or Plain), the button colour, the text and icon colour, the border, the colour under your finger, the corners and the border width, plus the colours of the selected button and of text fields and menus. A preview shows the result as you go. With only a button colour, Xenon picks a readable text colour for you. Deck keys keep their own key editor. Widgets from the Store run in a frame of their own, so they keep their look unless their maker uses these colours: Xenon now hands them over, and the SDK guide shows how (theme.controls).

  • Vitals reminders on macOS and Linux (Beta)

    The full-screen reminder that asks you to take a break now shows on the main screen of the Xenon app on macOS and Linux too, or as a system notification when the app is not open. "Minimize the other windows" works on macOS, on Linux with X11 and on KDE; on GNOME with Wayland the option is hidden and Settings says why. Not yet tried on real Mac and Linux machines.

  • Bit the pet is the same Bit as everywhere else

    The Vitals pet now uses the same face and moves as Bit in the chat, thanks you when you fill a meter and greets you when you come back. Its menu has "Talk to Bit", which opens the chat with Bit.

  • Breaks count by themselves

    When you are away from the PC for a while, the Stamina and Focus meters fill up when you come back, because you already took the break. Turn it off in Settings → Vitals if you prefer to mark them yourself.

  • Choose when Bit sleeps

    Bit stayed quiet from 23:00 to 7:00. Now you pick the hours in Settings → Vitals, or ask Bit, for example 18:00 to 9:00 to keep it quiet outside your working day.

  • One missed day no longer ends your streak

    Your Vitals streak keeps going if you skip a single day; it starts again only after two days in a row without a refill.

  • A cleaner Vitals tile

    Easier-to-read text, "Level 3" instead of a small badge, the time you spent at the PC today (time away does not count), and a countdown under the top bar chip before the PC locks.

  • Xenon is ready sooner after you turn on the PC

    On Windows it starts about two seconds earlier at sign-in. The first readings no longer wait for the slowest sensor: what is known appears at once and the rest fills in, so on our test PC everything was on screen after about two seconds instead of four and a half. The dashboard also keeps its files until they really change, so it opens in about half the time on the next start.

  • Nothing heavy runs while the PC is starting

    The file index starts 90 seconds after Xenon, or at once when you search for something, and other background jobs wait their turn. On Windows, Xenon starts half as many small programs in its first seconds.

  • A game gets your PC

    With Game mode on, while Xenon sees a game running the file index and the disk scans stop, and the other checks slow down: the volume of other apps every 32 seconds, batteries every 5 minutes, the list of running apps every 6 seconds. On Windows a notification can arrive up to 5 seconds later, unless Calls is on. All of it picks up again when you leave the game.

  • Background readers stay out of your way

    The programs that read sensors, media and the rest now run below normal priority on Windows, macOS and Linux, so whatever you are using comes first.

  • The dashboard draws less for nothing

    Animations on pages you are not looking at, and on background effects you turned off, no longer ask for new frames, and the colon of the clock now ticks in steps. A quiet dashboard costs less to keep on screen.

  • A shortcut held by another app costs less

    Xenon now tries again less and less often, up to every 5 minutes, so the shortcut can take that long to work after you close the other app.

  • Tab groups no longer redraw the whole dashboard

    Every tab group used to ask for all the tiles to be drawn again each time the layout was applied, so switching a tab got slower with each group you added. On a test dashboard with five groups that work went from 172 ms to 43 ms in a browser. The widget palette and the Deck key editor no longer redraw the dashboard behind them when they open, and a tab whose custom widget has no package yet says "Custom widget" instead of "custom".

  • Fewer calls while the page starts

    Lyrics and Dev cleanup ask once whether they are unlocked instead of at every redraw, which leaves 30 fewer calls to the local server in the first 6 seconds of a load (105 before, 75 now).

  • Lighter on Linux and macOS

    Disks are read at most every 30 seconds instead of at every sensor reading, so free space can be up to 30 seconds behind. On Linux, finding the window in front takes one command fewer every 2 seconds, a desktop without xprop looks for it every 5 minutes instead of every 2 seconds, and a PC without an NVIDIA card no longer tries nvidia-smi at every reading.

  • The Windows helper starts faster and uses less memory

    The small program behind media, audio, notifications and search used to prepare itself again at every start, in each of its processes. It now comes ready: a start takes about a third of the CPU, and the parts that stay running use about a fifth less memory. The file grows from 12 to 26 MB.

  • Performance Mode no longer starts PowerShell

    Starting and ending a session used to open five PowerShell processes, and a running session opened another every five minutes to check on the game: about 30 in a two-hour game. Xenon now reads the process list and sets priority itself, and reads the power plan with Windows' own powercfg. Reading the power plan went from about 730 ms to 15 ms, the app numbers on the sheet from about 1.3 s to under 0.4 s, and the check on the game from about 730 ms to 3 ms. PowerShell stays only as a fallback. During a game in a session, Xenon also reads audio, batteries and the app list less often, even with Game Mode turned off.

Security

  • Websites can no longer read your PC's data

    Any site you visited could ask Xenon for what is playing, your notes, audio apps, network and PC numbers, and the name of the game or app in front, through an old route kept for iCUE widgets. Now a site can learn only that Xenon is on, and the iCUE widget keeps working.

  • Widgets and animated backgrounds have one less way out

    They already had no network, but WebRTC, the browser's call technology, slipped past that rule, and a widget could also send its page to a Google address. Both are closed for every widget. If you made a widget that used WebRTC, it will no longer work.

  • A paired phone can no longer spend or change what your PC pays with

    Buying with Sparks and saving a supporter or Sparks code now work only on the PC, and the phone says so. A phone can still unlock what you already own.

  • A full security review

    Every part of Xenon was checked: what a web page can reach, paired phones, the assistant's tools, widgets and shared presets, saved passwords, downloads and the app itself. Thanks to jarnix for the report that started it. What changes for you:

    • Other websites can no longer reach Xenon. A page in your browser can open the dashboard through a link and nothing else: it cannot run anything, read anything or show Xenon inside its own page. The dashboard, the iCUE widgets and the tools on your PC (the MCP bridge, the Claude Code hooks, webhooks) work as before.
    • A paired phone or tablet runs the keys you built. It still controls media, volume, lights, timers and everything else it did, and it presses every Deck key you set up on the PC. It cannot invent new actions that open programs, type text or call out, nor add such keys to the Deck. It can remove your favourite apps or change their order, but new favourites are added at the PC, because a favourite is an app the phone may start. Setting up remote desktop, PC Control and backups is done at the PC. A device unused for 90 days has to be paired again, and the PC shows a notice whenever a new device pairs.
    • The assistant stays within what you ask. It opens apps, websites and documents but not scripts or network locations, closes one app by name, does not unlock doors, disarm alarms or open the garage, calls only your contacts or a number you gave it, and does not put script or typed text keys on the Deck. A custom news feed address is added by you in Settings, on the Stocks, Football & News page. When a Claude Code or Codex command is too long to show in full on the card, the approval goes back to the terminal.
    • Widgets keep only what you approved. A widget that tries to load another page is stopped, a shared widget can no longer replace one you installed without asking, and shared Deck keys cannot type text by chaining single keys. A widget can load code only from its own folder, so it can no longer read what is playing or your PC's load without the permission for it.
    • Bit asks before starting a program through a Deck action. The same card you see for other sensitive actions now appears when Bit wants to run a program with its own arguments or a Store app that way. "Open Spotify" still works straight away, and text that arrives from notes, tasks, feeds or web pages is treated as something to read, never as an order.
    • Saved passwords stay with their address. If the address of Home Assistant, UniFi, OBS or Streamer.bot changes, the saved token or password is not sent to the new one: type it again. Private calendar links are no longer sent to the screens that show your settings. A backup file still holds them, so keep it private.
    • What Xenon downloads and runs is verified. The one tap install of the Xenon app checks the signed release list first, and Whisper, PresentMon and the Browser tile's ad blocker are pinned to a checked version.
    • Opening files is safer. Types that run code when opened (management consoles, compiled help, Python scripts, disk images and others) are not opened by an Open file key on Windows; a Run script key still runs a Python script. Files received from a phone carry the same mark as a download, so Windows checks them when opened.
    • The old Xeneon Edge Hub iCUE widget no longer shows the agenda. Its calendar was readable by any web page. The current Xenon iCUE widget shows the whole dashboard, calendar included.
    • Libraries with known issues are updated. The secure connection library the Xenon app uses for its updates, and three libraries under Bit's voice.
  • A paired phone keeps to what it is for

    Bit on a phone no longer calls, texts or runs a command on the PC, and it opens only your favourite apps or an app on a Deck key. The Smart Home tile on a phone still drives lights and comfort, while locks, alarms, covers and scripts answer only on the PC. A phone can take a permission away from a widget but no longer give one, and it cannot start a new Claude Code run. Answering a decision of a run started on the PC still works.

  • A paired phone can no longer sign this PC in to Tailscale

    It could start the sign-in and read its link, and whoever opens that link puts the PC on their own network. The sign-in now happens at the PC, and the link is no longer sent to a phone.

Fixed

  • Updating from 4.11 finishes on every Windows build

    On some Windows 11 builds the update could leave the old version running, check for the new one, find the old one and undo itself. Xenon 5.0 now stops the old version again, in a way those builds always see, before it installs anything, so the update goes through.

  • Adding a widget keeps you on the page you are on

    Opening Add widget on a later page could send the dashboard back to the first one: the panel reloaded every widget on screen, and a widget that puts the cursor in a field when it starts (such as a password box) pulled the dashboard to its page. The panel now only reads the list again, and a widget on a page you are not looking at can no longer move the dashboard.

  • The clock island keeps its place in the tiles after you add a widget

    On a later page, adding a widget made the island lie on top of the tiles under it instead of cutting into them, until the dashboard was reloaded: it measured itself against the first page instead of the one in view.

  • An SDK widget opened to full screen covers the whole screen again

    With the Liquid Glass look, an expanded widget stayed inside its own tile with the clock island over it. It now fills the screen as before.

  • The tiles take the island's shape as it appears

    When the dashboard opens, the clock island grows from a small dot once the loading screen has gone, and the tiles open their cutouts with it, instead of showing up already cut. When you change page, the tiles hold still while the page slides, and the cutout opens slowly once the page has stopped under the island. The space around the island is now the same on both sides. Their content slides down smoothly. With reduced motion on, in performance mode or during a game, the island and the cutouts simply appear, with no animation.

  • A widget's questions can be read on the desktop

    With Liquid Glass, the window that asks for a widget's permissions on the desktop was almost see-through, with the open windows sharp behind the words. There it is now solid.

  • A widget imported from the Xenon menu goes on the screen

    Importing a widget from the menu's Widgets section (Your widgets, Import) only added it to Installed, so it had to be added again from there. It now goes in a free spot on the screen at once, as one picked from the Add list does.

  • No leftover file in the Temp folder when reading sound devices fails

    On Windows, when the list of sound devices took too long, Xenon left a small file in the system Temp folder each time. It now removes it.

  • Drop-down lists match Liquid Glass, and their search box can be read

    On Liquid Glass the lists that open from a field (the Deck's actions, its profiles, Bit's attach menu and every other drop-down) now wear the same glass edge as the windows they open from, with a neutral mark on the chosen row instead of green. The search box at the top of a long list let the rows scrolling under it show through, so what you typed was hard to read: it now covers them, on every look.

  • A single Spotify song plays in the Spotify app

    Playing one song from a Deck key, from Bit, from a search or from a widget could show Spotify as playing while the Spotify app on the computer loaded nothing. Xenon now starts the song inside its album, so it plays at once and the rest of the album follows. A song picked inside a playlist still carries on through that playlist.

  • Hold to allow fits its key on a phone

    When Claude Code or Codex asks for something that cannot be undone, the key you hold to allow it took three lines on a phone in Italian, Spanish, Dutch and Russian. Its words are shorter now and take two at most.

  • An incoming call can be closed on a phone held sideways

    On a paired phone turned sideways the call card hid Close and the line that says why a call cannot be answered from Xenon, and a phone has no Esc key: the card went away only by answering, declining or waiting for the ring to end. Both are back, under the caller and under the keys. On small phones held sideways the card now lies down as well, instead of running past the bottom of the screen.

  • The Twitch chat drops "Waiting for the first message" when messages arrive

    In the Twitch tile you watch on, that line could stay above a chat that was already talking until something else redrew the tile. It now goes with the first message.

  • OBS without a preview shows its message, not an empty box

    When OBS was not set up, or had not sent its first picture yet, the preview drew an empty picture frame and squeezed "Configure OBS in Settings" into a strip beside it. The message now has the whole preview, on every look.

  • The File transfer title no longer touches the tile's edge

    The title and the size beside it sat against the border, and the files did not line up under the title. They now have the same margin as the other tiles, on every look.

  • "How it works" in the File transfer tile hides the files under it

    With Panel opacity below 100%, the list showed through the steps and neither could be read. The panel is now solid.

  • On a short File transfer tile the keys stay under the files

    With files in a short tile, the line and the two keys under the list could slide up over the last files. They now keep their room, and the list scrolls.

  • Closing a game no longer leaves Xenon thinking you still play

    When a game closed, the window in front could become the NVIDIA overlay or the Xbox Game Bar, and Xenon took it for a game that never ended: the file index and disk scans stayed paused, updates waited and Game Companion stayed on until the PC restarted. These overlays are no longer read as games.

  • The FPS counter no longer stays blank for the rest of a game after the dashboard comes back

    Xenon stopped reading frames 45 seconds after the last dashboard closed or lost its connection, and a game can refuse to let a new frame reader start while it runs: a dashboard that came back mid-game then showed no FPS until the game closed. During a game, the reader that is already running now stays on.

  • A stray Enter no longer approves anything

    A copy to the clipboard, a pairing, an incoming call, a Deck key's request and Bit's confirm cards all open with the keyboard on the window, not on a key.

  • Lyrics no longer goes blank

    If the language changed, a trial ended or the tile was copied with its options open, the tile stayed empty until you reloaded.

  • The phone's Back key stays in Xenon in Send to PC

    It closes How it works first and the sheet after it, as Esc does. Before, it left Xenon.

  • A file's age in Send to PC is in your language

    It read "1 g" in every language.

  • The request window for Codex and Claude Code is readable on light themes

    A Codex request can no longer be covered by the screensaver or a promo.

  • A widget that asks only for AI or Island activities

    no longer tells you it asks for nothing, and a pairing is no longer held up or closed by a permission question.

  • The Set key on the menu's search shortcut works

    It did nothing, and now opens Settings. With the menu open on the dashboard, Tab stays inside, and on a phone the X stays in the corner.

  • Long words fit on a phone

    Today in the weather's days and the labels of the bottom bar were cut in Russian, French, Dutch, Portuguese, German and Italian. The tile and the window now give the day its room, and each key of the bar is as wide as its word.

  • On a Comic theme the first question shows one main key

    Both keys were the same green.

  • Words on the Deck and the music keys are readable on Comic themes

    They took the colour of the lines, which is dim on Auto, and on a light theme the play key had almost vanished.

  • Typing a Smart Profiles rule is safe

    The words were thrown away when the list of apps arrived.

  • The Deck's confirm card appears on the alerts and search windows too

    It was silently dropped there.

  • Enter on an empty Game Companion box

    no longer starts a look that can cost Sparks, and Recharge opens the Sparks in the menu's window instead of a stray browser window.

  • Change my cookie choice works from the keyboard

    The privacy page's key now takes you to the box and back.

  • GIGABYTE boards follow iCUE from the first minute

    After a power-on with GIGABYTE Control Center closed, the board and the fans on its headers could stay on a rainbow and ignore every colour. Xenon now wakes the board by itself when iCUE finds it and after sleep. Nothing is saved on the board, and with direct control on, or with the board switched off in Lighting, it does nothing.

  • A restart or an update replaces the running engine on every Windows build

    On Windows 11 build 26300 the port table reports a listening socket under a different state from one read to the next, so the launcher and the updater could miss the running engine: the old one stayed, and the new one stopped with "port 3030 is already in use". Both now find it the same way the launcher already checks the port.

  • Swiping between pages works on top of widgets

    A finger dragged sideways on a list in Claude, Codex, ChatGPT, Football, Twitch, YouTube, Lyrics, Streamer.bot, the disk widgets or Bit's chat did nothing, so you had to find an empty spot of the screen. The lists still scroll up and down as before.

  • Widgets you make keep the page swipe

    Bit and the widget checks now warn when a widget would stop the sideways drag that changes page, and say how to fix it. The widget guide explains it too.

  • The loading screen speaks your language

    Everything Xenon says while it starts, including the start and repair messages, was always in English. It now follows the language you chose, in all 11, and on a first launch the language of your system. A normal start now shows only Bit, from the first moment to the dashboard: words appear only when the start is taking longer than it should.

  • The animated wallpaper stays on when you take a screenshot

    The Snipping Tool's overlay was read as a full-screen app, so the wallpaper disappeared and did not come back, and with widgets kept out of captures the desktop came out black in the picture. The wallpaper now stays on and shows in your screenshots, and it also comes back when a full-screen window closes and a Xenon window takes the focus.

  • The real desktop no longer flashes when an app opens or closes

    The animated wallpaper hid the moment a window filled the screen, so the picture under it showed through for an instant. It now stops only once the app has finished opening, and comes back as the app closes.

  • Bit stands alone in every icon

    The dark square behind Bit is gone from the app icon, the taskbar, the tray, the Store tile, the favicons and the logo on the site, and Bit is larger in them. On a light browser tab Bit turns the deeper green so it stays easy to see. Only the iPhone home screen icon keeps its ground, because iOS would paint it black anyway.

  • Choose which screens show the animated wallpaper

    In the Xenon menu, Look has a new Screens row: one screen, some or all of them, for the wallpaper and the screensaver. Automatic stays the screens without the dashboard. A chosen screen that is unplugged is skipped, and you can ask Bit: "put the wallpaper on screens 1 and 3".

  • Scene used shows a live preview

    In the Xenon menu a small picture plays the chosen scene, and the one under the pointer before you pick it.

  • The animated wallpaper can show your own backgrounds

    The animated backgrounds of your saved themes were missing from Scene used, so only Classic and Store scenes could be picked. They are now in the list in the menu and in Settings, and Bit can choose them by name.

  • The Keys page of the Xenon menu lists the search and page shortcuts

    Open search (Alt+Space) and the page shortcuts from Settings were missing there; they now show with their combination and whether they are active.

  • Bold words in Codex and ChatGPT answers can be read on a light look

    They were white on a pale background inside the two widgets.

  • Remote Control keeps its setup

    The setup disappeared as soon as Sunshine and Tailscale were installed, even with steps still to do. It now stays until you finish, and the control panel has Open the setup.

  • The Remote Control key that unpairs everything says so

    "Kill-switch (disconnect now)" removed every paired device, not only the connection. It is now called Remove all devices.

  • Remote Control speaks your language

    About 20 status messages were written only in Italian. They now come in every language of the app.

  • Context profiles stay inside the page

    Their table ran past the edge of the page. Each activity is now a row you open.

  • Settings no longer offer what your system cannot do

    Off Windows, the power plan, process priority and closing background apps cannot work, and the power plan, on by default, reported a failure each time: they are now hidden and skipped there, in the optimize sheet too. The two switches that mirror notifications did nothing on macOS and Hide during Remote Desktop did nothing off Windows, so they are gone there. Start Ollama when you sign in no longer shows on Linux, and on every system the lines about notifications, the Notifications tile and the graphics tip no longer name Windows or the Xeneon Edge where it is not true.

  • Smart Home lists work on the Xeneon Edge

    Its dropdowns opened blank there. They now use the same lists as the rest of the app.

  • Messages lead to the right place in Settings

    Error messages, Bit's answers and the guides on the site named pages that were renamed or never existed, such as "Settings → Game mode" and "Settings → Backup". They now use the names you see in the list, in every language.

  • Two widgets in the same corner no longer sit on top of each other

    Choose a corner that is taken and the new widget goes right beside what is there, with room between them. A widget you drag by hand stays exactly where you drop it. The Widget section also says the truth for a widget in the middle or on an edge, instead of naming a corner it is not in.

  • Lyrics: the free trial button works on a widget on the screen

    It did nothing there; it now opens the trial page.

  • Widgets now reach the corner you pick on every monitor

    On a screen with a different scale from the main one, the widget layer stopped at two thirds of the screen, so top right looked like top centre and bottom right like the middle. It now covers the whole screen.

  • Moving a widget with the mouse is safer

    Passing over another widget no longer turns the two into tabs: you have to stop on it, and Xenon says when letting go will make tabs. A new Put it back button undoes everything since you started moving things, and a widget in tabs has a Separate button in its screen in the menu. The frame around the Game performance words now has their real size, and its buttons sit beside them.

  • Drag a widget right in its picture

    In the menu, the picture of the screen now shows the widget itself, at its real size, with no window behind it. Drag it anywhere, or tap a corner.

  • Music buttons work when Windows' media list is stuck

    Pause, next and previous used to do nothing, with no message, whenever that Windows service stopped answering or a player had never joined it. Xenon now presses the keyboard's media key instead.

  • Gains and losses are easy to read again

    With Windows or macOS in light mode, a dark Xenon drew the green and red of Stocks, the ticker and football too dark for its tiles. They now follow the look of Xenon instead of the system.

  • The Calendar stays readable in small tiles

    In a short or narrow tile the weeks squeezed together until numbers ran into each other and the event dots sat on top of the dates. Rows now keep their height, the dots have a lane of their own, the events scroll instead of pushing the month away, and the header wraps on a narrow tile. The same holds at a high Zoom, up to 200% and beyond: Zoom makes a tile narrower for the text inside it, so there the month shortens to "Nov" and stays on one line with its buttons, leaving more room for the events.

  • Signal calls ring on the dashboard

    Signal is now in the apps allowed to ring, on by default, wherever Xenon can read the app's notifications. Its voice calls have their own wording, so Xenon had to learn that in every language Signal uses. The card shows who is calling and can open Signal; answering happens in Signal itself, as with WhatsApp.

  • Softer graph lines in the light theme

    The grid behind the graphs in the System tile looked like ruled paper.

  • No more thin line on album covers

    Some covers showed a coloured hairline along one edge.

  • News headlines show in full

    With more stories than the tile could hold, every row got squeezed and a headline on two lines lost its second line halfway through. Rows now keep their height and the list scrolls.

  • Discord and YouTube fit narrow tiles

    The last Discord tab is no longer cut, and YouTube's close button stays on the same row as the other controls.

  • YouTube's controls follow light themes

    The bar over the video stayed dark and hard to read.

  • Small labels in Weather and Football are easier to read

    The secondary text on those tiles was too pale.

  • Create in Xenon Maker sits straight

    In Settings the link was underlined and off centre, unlike the buttons next to it.

  • Xenon comes back on its own screen after a KVM switch

    When a monitor goes away, Windows can minimize the windows on the screens that stay. The Edge then showed the desktop until you picked Automatic in the tray, because the dashboard has no taskbar button to bring it back with. Xenon now notices within a few seconds and returns to its screen by itself, without taking the focus from what you are doing.

  • Playback and the music condition work with any app that has sound

    Windows keeps a list of what is playing, and that list can stop answering, while many players never join it. Either way Xenon saw nothing, so a Playback widget set to show only with music stayed hidden while the music played. Xenon now also looks at which apps have sound open, on Windows and Linux. Calls, mixers and capture tools do not count, and neither does the game you are playing. While Windows' list is not answering, the play and pause buttons cannot reach the app.

  • The FAQ now says what a small payment does

    A payment under 5 USD is a plain tip: it opens nothing and brings no Sparks.

  • An old supporter code no longer hides your Sparks

    If the saved code stopped working, Bit and the Store now use the Sparks code saved beside it instead of failing.

  • Put back everything you tried, not just one thing

    After the trial, the welcome card stays open until the last item is back.

  • The picture on the buy sheet is no longer cut

    A picture far from the frame's shape is now shown whole.

  • Sparks codes now get an order email

    Buying with a Sparks code sends one, as a supporter code does, and a code email that failed is sent again by itself.

  • Xenon no longer closes by itself when a game starts

    The reading of PlayStation controllers could crash inside an old part of Windows when a game changed the list of devices, and it took the whole app with it, widgets included. That reading now runs in a small process of its own: if it falls, Xenon stays open and starts it again. It only runs with a PlayStation controller connected.

  • FPS stay on when a game runs behind the overlay or out of focus

    With a widget above it, or after a click elsewhere, Windows can start composing a game instead of letting it flip straight to the screen, and Xenon dropped those frames as if they came from an ordinary app, so the overlay showed no FPS at all. Frames of the game Xenon is already tracking now count however they reach the screen.

  • Nothing white behind a notification as it closes

    On the window that shows notifications over your other apps, a closing card faded out on a see-through window and could leave a white shape behind it for a moment. There a card now goes at once, with no closing animation. Its opening animation stays.
