  • The search bar follows your theme and takes the keyboard at once

    The bar opened by the shortcut read your look only once, and missed it: it now reads it every time it opens, light, retro and comic included, and text fields no longer show a box inside the bar. On Windows the bar could also open without the keyboard, because the shortcut reaches a helper and not Xenon itself. It now takes the focus every time, so you can type straight away, on the first press after launch too.

  • A widget set to show only while you play stays when you click away

    On the lighter widget pages, "while playing" followed the window in front, so the widget vanished as soon as you clicked outside the game. It now stays for as long as the game is running.

  • The optimization card asks once per game run

    The "game detected" card came back every time you returned to the game. It now asks once, and again only the next time you start that game.

  • The performance widget no longer apologises

    While a game ran with no frames to read, the widget said its frame rate could not be read. The numbers come back by themselves, so it now says nothing, and speaks only when the reader is missing and you can install it.

  • Notifications on the main screen have no dark box behind them

    The shadow of a card was cut by the edge of its window and showed as a dark rectangle. Cards on the main screen now have no shadow.

  • The picture of In-game performance shows what you get

    In Add it showed the dashboard panel with a graph. It now shows the words as they sit over a game.

  • No error where the system has no web audio

    On a WebKit built without audio, the sound code failed while the page opened. It now stays silent instead.

  • Discord, Twitch and YouTube stay linked through a hiccup

    If one of them had a brief problem while Xenon renewed its access, Xenon dropped the link and you had to connect your account again in Settings. Now the link goes only when the service says the access is really revoked; otherwise Xenon keeps it and tries again.

  • Transparent widgets stay transparent on every background

    A widget that declared a dark color-scheme and a transparent background showed a solid dark block behind it, so it could not be made to look like words on the screen. Xenon now matches the widget's frame to what the widget declares, on load and whenever it changes.

  • Bit's eyes are the same size again

    At some screen zooms, such as 125% or 150%, one of Bit's eyes came out wider than the other in the small icons: the Ask Bit button, Settings and the emails. Bit is now drawn so that both eyes stay even at any zoom.

  • Share links open again

    Opening a link to a theme, a widget or a page in Xenon (one with #preset= in it) was refused as an invalid code, so the only way in was pasting the code by hand. The link now goes straight to the import.

  • An uninstalled widget leaves your screen

    Uninstalling a Store widget that was on the screen left an empty box behind. It now goes with the widget.

  • A Deck switch shows the truth when one of its steps fails

    A key that turned your lights off and then failed on a later step (for example a light that is not connected right now) jumped back to "on", so the next tap ran the off action again. Now the key stays where it moved, and the message says that light is not available instead of showing a code.

  • Lights switched off from a key stay off after a restart

    The key also shows it: it reads off, and the lights stay dark, until you switch them on.

  • Motherboard lighting asks the chip less

    Xenon looked for self-reporting fans on every empty output at each start, and the chip writes to its own memory every time it does that. Each output is now looked at once, and again only when you press Search again.

  • Two devices of the same model each get their own battery

    Two identical mice or headphones used to share one row, so one hid the other. They now read like "PRO X 2" and "PRO X 2 (2)", for Logitech and Corsair devices and for anything on Bluetooth.

  • A sleeping mouse no longer looks like a fresh reading

    A device that stopped answering keeps its last level, now dimmed, with how long ago it was read in the Batteries widget. Widgets and Xenon Maker can tell the same, and Bit says so when you ask.

  • The switches in the tray menu work again

    Keep games focused, Keep mouse on its screen, Fullscreen and Match render GPU to screen could not be turned on or off from the tray icon: every click was undone at once, so the checkmark never moved. Reported on Discord.

  • Tasks and calendar events no longer disappear when you use more than one screen

    The Tasks tile and the calendar saved their whole list, so a screen with an older list deleted what a phone, another screen or Bit had added in the meantime, and a screen that could not load the list at startup could replace the whole agenda with the one event you added. Each change now travels on its own and the PC applies it to the list it really has, every screen updates by itself when something changes elsewhere, and a change made while the PC is unreachable is sent again until it arrives, with a note on screen if it takes a while. Repeating tasks also come back on time on a screen that stays on all day, instead of only after a reload.

  • A damaged settings file no longer turns into the factory settings

    If the file that holds your layout, theme and pages could not be read, some changes (a watchlist symbol, a news feed, a setting Bit changed) started again from the factory settings and saved them over everything. They now stop instead, and a file another program holds for a moment is simply read again. Xenon also keeps a copy a day of your settings, Deck, notes, tasks, calendar and timers for the last seven days, and if one of them cannot be read at startup it puts back the newest good copy, keeps the damaged file aside and tells you on screen. When there is no copy yet, a damaged task, calendar, note, Deck or timer file is kept aside and that part starts again empty, while the settings file is never written over.

  • No more white background after a KVM switch or a monitor coming and going

    With a custom theme, switching the monitor to another computer and back could leave Xenon on the Edge with a bright white background behind the tiles until it was restarted, dark themes included. Two things met. A theme's animated background is often paused (when nobody touches the screen, during games, and all the time on PCs with two graphics cards), so it is one picture drawn and left alone, and a screen leaving can reset the graphics card, which wipes that picture; nothing drew it again. And behind that empty picture the browser painted plain white instead of the theme's own colour. The background now draws itself again when it is wiped and whenever the screens change, and if it is ever empty, the theme's colour shows behind it, not white. Reported on Discord.

  • Open Discord works on macOS and Linux

    The button on the Discord widget that starts Discord when it is closed only ever worked on Windows: elsewhere it did nothing. It now starts the app on all three, and on Linux it finds a normal install, a Flatpak or a Snap.

  • A Deck shortcut no longer takes the focus away from your game

    (#142). A key that sends a keyboard shortcut (a TeamSpeak soundboard key, for example) pressed while a game ran full screen gave the focus to some other app on Windows. Xenon assumed the window in front was always the dashboard you had just tapped and sent the shortcut to the window behind it; with Keep games focused on, or from a paired phone, the window in front is the game itself. The shortcut now goes to the window in front unless that window is Xenon, and a window that already has the focus is left alone. macOS and Linux already worked this way.

  • Win+D no longer hides Xenon from its own screen

    (#143). Show desktop raised the desktop over the Xenon app on the Edge, or on any screen where it runs full screen, until you brought another app back. While the desktop is in front, the app now stays above it, without taking the focus, and goes back to normal the moment you open anything else, so pressing Win+D again still brings your apps back. A Xenon window on a screen you share with other apps is hidden by Win+D as before. Windows only: macOS and Linux handle Show desktop their own way.

  • The Browser tile recovers by itself when the hidden browser stops answering

    (#144). After a while the Browser tiles could stay on their loading animation for good, also when the dashboard was opened in a normal browser, until the background browser was ended by hand. Xenon waited for it forever. Now a request that gets no answer fails after a time limit, Xenon checks whether the browser is still alive, and restarts it if not; the tile opens again on its own. A page that is merely slow does not restart anything.

  • Audio devices with ö, ä, ü or any non-English name can be switched to from the Deck

    (#145). On a German Windows the headphones are called Kopfhörer, and a key switching to them did nothing, with no error. Xenon read the device list from SoundVolumeView in the wrong character encoding, so the name it sent back named no device. The list is now read as UTF-8, which also keeps Japanese, Korean, Polish or Czech names intact, and keys you already made switch correctly without setting them up again.

  • The browser no longer opens at sign-in next to the Xenon app

    On some PCs Chrome (or your default browser) opened the dashboard every time you signed in to Windows, while the Xenon app itself appeared minutes later. The app had switched on "open in the browser at startup" by itself, and the browser was opened before Xenon was even ready. Now that option is only set from a real browser, it never opens a tab when the Xenon app starts with Windows, and it waits until Xenon answers instead of showing an error page.

  • Bit remembers what it did a moment ago

    After saving a clip or running any other action, Bit could say on the next message that it had not really done it, because the chat kept only its words and not the actions behind them. Each reply now keeps a short note of the actions it ran and how they ended, so Bit stands by what it did. The note holds only the action names, never file names or what you typed, and you never see it.

  • Vitals and Bit now remember what you tap on a widget on your screen

    Refilling a meter, a truce with Bit or his streak on a Vitals widget placed on the desktop or as an overlay was lost on the next reload. It is now saved and shows on your other screens too.

  • The animated wallpaper no longer stays on the screen after you turn it off

    On Windows the last picture of the scene could stay on the desktop until something redrew it. Xenon now asks Windows to redraw the desktop when the wallpaper closes, and your own wallpaper comes back.

  • The keyboard focus ring shows again

    With the Tab key or a controller you could not see which button or switch was selected in Settings, the Store, the gallery and the Xenon menu, because a theme value since 4.6.0 replaced the ring with a plain colour that browsers ignore. The ring now shows on every theme.

  • Voicemeeter widgets get the mixer

    Widgets that draw the Voicemeeter strips and buses received nothing, because the dashboard never passed the mixer on to them. They now get it, including the current state as soon as they open, and widgets made in the Xenon Maker can show each strip, each bus, the gain and where a strip sends its sound.

  • Bit's voice mode starts again after you cancel it

    If you tapped the voice button and tapped it again to cancel before the microphone was ready, the recording stayed open in the background, so the next tap and the chat microphone did nothing for about five minutes. Cancelling now lets the microphone go, and the next tap records.

  • The GPU temperature shows again on NVIDIA cards

    NVIDIA driver 621.01 started reporting the temperature with decimals (52.56 instead of 52), and Xenon read that as no temperature at all, so it was missing from every widget. Xenon now reads every NVIDIA reading with or without decimals, and if the driver gives no temperature it takes it from the card's own sensor instead. Reported on Discord.

  • The Windows app no longer asks to install Xenon again after a restart

    When Xenon was installed but had not started yet, for example on a slow first start after turning the PC on, the app showed "Xenon isn't finished installing" after 20 seconds. Its setup then said Xenon was already installed and to restart the PC, and the restart led back to the same screen. Now the app knows Xenon is installed: it waits longer, then offers Start Xenon. If Xenon still does not start, Repair Xenon shows the reason Xenon wrote down, starts it again and, if that is not enough, installs it again with your settings, layouts and notes kept. Also, on a Windows account that is not an administrator, setup no longer asks for an administrator's password: installing with it put the start at sign-in on the administrator's account, so Xenon worked until the next restart and then asked to be installed again. Reported on Discord.

  • The FPS reading no longer drops out after you close and reopen the dashboard quickly

    Xenon stops its frame reader when no dashboard is open and starts it again when one connects. When that happened within a moment, the reader that was closing could switch the new one off and start a third, and the two then fought over the same Windows frame tracing, so game detection and the FPS number could go blank for a while. Only the reader that is running now counts.

  • The Deck key Lights on/off now really switches the lights off

    Off used to hand the lights back to iCUE and to the motherboard, which then showed their own colours, and a colour map from the Lighting page or the album colour kept painting, so often only one device changed. Off now turns every light Xenon drives dark, the map and the music colour included, until you press the key again, switch the lights on in Settings, or a key sets a colour. Bit does the same when you ask it to switch the lights off.

  • A second copy of Xenon no longer takes over your Claude Code or Codex link

    Xenon fixes an incomplete Claude Code or Codex link by itself when it starts. A second copy running on the same PC with its own data, for example a portable one on another port, also did it and pointed the link at itself, so the tile of your real Xenon stopped getting the sessions. Now only the copy that made the link repairs it.

  • On a Mac and on Linux, Ambient waits until you leave the PC, not only the dashboard

    The Ambient screensaver opened after the minutes you set without touching the dashboard, even while you were working on another screen, because Xenon read how long the whole PC had been idle only on Windows. It now reads it on a Mac and on Linux too (on Linux with xprintidle on X11, otherwise from the session), so Ambient opens when you are really away, and the meters that pause while you are away pause there too.

  • The Network element of an Ambient scene shows your speeds

    It always read "--", because the scene never received the network readings. It now shows download and upload as the System tile does.

  • The Lighting tile names your Corsair devices

    Its device list showed some iCUE devices as a long code in braces instead of their name. It now shows the same name as Settings, for example iCUE LINK H150i.

  • The Media wave shows on the Media tile you are looking at

    It was drawn only on the original Media tile, so with a copy of the tile, or with the original hidden or on another page, the wave never appeared at all. It now moves to the Media tile on screen.

  • The Media wave follows the app that is really playing

    With music or a video playing in a browser, the wave could follow another window whose name only looked like the browser (for example the Xenon app window itself) and stay flat. It now picks the app with the exact name, and the browser window that shows the service.

  • Settings says why the Media wave is not showing

    It used to say that Xenon Helper was running even when the wave was paused on purpose. Now it says the real reason: Performance Mode is on, a game is running, the lyrics are open, a window is still open in front, or the sound comes from a different app than the one the Media tile shows.

  • The "every N days" box of a task shows only when it is used

    In the Tasks tile, the box for the number of days stayed on screen for every repeat, even with no repeat or a daily one; it now appears only when you pick a custom repeat.

  • GIFs keep moving where you add them

    A GIF picked for an ambient scene, a Deck key or a Deck decoration came out still, because Xenon redrew it to make it smaller and kept only its first frame. It now stays as it is when it fits, and when it is too big it becomes a smaller GIF that still plays. Animated WebP and APNG pictures move too, and an animated background made in Xenon Maker plays a GIF on its picture layer. If an animation cannot fit at all, Xenon now tells you instead of quietly stopping it.

  • The install dialog of a widget names the Pages permission

    A widget that asks to switch dashboard pages showed the word "pages" in the install dialog, untranslated; it now says what the permission does, in your language.

  • The tutorial points at the right buttons again, and shows search and the Store

    With the minimal top bar the tutorial highlighted empty space past the edge of the screen, because Bit, Layout and Settings live in side bars that slide away; it now holds them open while it runs and puts them back as they were. On a phone it points at the buttons along the bottom, a tile on another page is skipped, and a tile further down the page is brought into view. It also has a new step for searching your PC, mentions the Store in Settings, says "tap +" instead of "drag" to add tiles, and its last card names the right place to replay it, Settings → General, in every language.

  • YouTube plays again in the Linux app

    In the desktop app on Linux the YouTube player in a tile stayed blank, because Xenon sent the player's own address to your browser instead of showing it in the tile. Only the player's embed address is now allowed to load in the tile; every other link still opens in your browser. Fixed by Tech127x on GitHub.

  • Settings no longer opens behind the lock screen

    If Settings was opened while the lock screen or an ambient scene was showing (by voice, from a paired phone or with a shortcut), the clock and the weather stayed drawn over the panel. Opening Settings now closes the lock screen first.

  • The desktop app picks up your home gesture and remote desktop settings at startup

    The dashboard tells the app about them once the page has finished loading, and in the desktop app that moment never came, because another message sent during loading cancelled it. A fresh start could keep the app's previous behaviour until you changed the setting again.

  • The assistant speaks again with Claude, Ollama, Sparks, Claude Code and Codex

    Microsoft changed how its free voice service is reached, and the spoken answer stayed silent for everyone not on Gemini or ChatGPT. Xenon uses the updated connection, and if a voice ever fails to play, the answer now still shows on screen instead of vanishing.

  • Talking to the assistant feels like a conversation

    After you tapped the voice button, the screen said Listening a good two seconds before the microphone was really recording, so the first words of what you said were lost and it often seemed not to hear you at all. Now it shows Opening microphone until it really listens. It also answers sooner: it waits about a second and a half after your last word instead of three, and understands what you said three times faster (about one second for a short request). The local transcription also stopped dropping the first word when you start talking right away: "che tempo fa domani" was heard as "tempo fa domani".

  • A voice conversation no longer shows up in the chat

    Starting the assistant with the voice button, the wake word or a Deck key used to write every spoken turn, and the listening prompts, into the text chat on your dashboard. The voice conversation now stays on the voice screen, errors included, and the chat keeps only what you typed there.

  • The unlock note is in your language

    The line under the code box that says your code is personal, and the message for a code that does not open this drop, appeared in English in every language. They are now translated.

  • Notifications leave without an empty bar

    When a notification closed in the Dynamic Island, its glass shrank into an empty capsule before the clock came back, and with Settings or another window open the empty capsule stayed floating on top before vanishing. Now the clock fades in on the glass as it shrinks, so it lands already filled, and when the clock is hidden or covered the notification draws in and fades out where it is.

  • A paired phone can no longer remove your supporter code

    Forget it, in Settings and in Import, now works only on the PC itself. On a paired phone or tablet it says the code can only be removed on the PC, and the code stays saved. Settings and Import also no longer say the code was removed when the removal did not go through.

  • Someone else's background stays theirs in a theme you tweak

    Saving a look built on an imported animated background now keeps it marked as imported, so it is removed together with that content. Sharing a tweaked theme still works, but it leaves out an animated background or font that came from someone else, and says so.

  • The right message after too many unlock attempts

    When you tried a supporter or item code many times in a row, Import said it couldn't reach the unlock service, which sent you looking for a network problem. It now says there were too many attempts and to try again in a few minutes. Reported on Discord.

  • Nothing covers the phone's bottom bar when the ticker is at the bottom

    On a phone with the scrolling ticker along the bottom edge, the Discord invite, the game pill, Deck and event messages and the Customize bar panel landed on the bottom bar by the ticker's height. They now sit above both.

  • Tight tiles stay tidy

    When the System tile is narrow, its tabs (System, Volume, Microphone, History) no longer stack into a column: they stay on one row and show only their icons when the names do not fit. On narrow cards the drive label no longer breaks in two under the free space, and the GPU temperature no longer covers the GPU name. In the Deck key editor on a phone, the five Behaviour buttons sit in even rows instead of breaking at random widths, and Save, Save as preset, Delete and Cancel fit on screen in every language.

  • Text colour and second colour on a Deck key that is on

    In a key's On tab, a second colour picked without a first one was thrown away, so the gradient never appeared; it now fades from the key's own colour. In the Comic theme, the text colour of a key, on or off, was always black whatever you picked, and the icon size (S, M, L) did nothing; both work now.

  • Finished tasks on an Ambient scene

    A Tasks element showed finished tasks as still to do, and its option to show finished tasks did nothing. Both work now.

  • A large Ambient scene you import is still there after a restart

    A scene shared with its pictures inside could be a few MB, but Xenon kept only scenes up to 400 KB when it saved your settings, so the import said it worked and the scene was gone the next time Xenon started. Scenes up to the size a share code can carry are now kept. When there is no more room, the import says so before you press Import and tells you to delete a scene you no longer use.

  • Ambient scene elements show their own text colour and rounded panel

    In an Ambient scene, the text colour chosen in an element's style was ignored and its panel always had square corners. Both now show as chosen, and the corners follow the theme's roundness.

  • The background picture of a widget shows

    A picture or gradient chosen in Widget style → Background stayed hidden behind the widget's own panel on most tiles, so nothing seemed to change. It now replaces the panel's fill, with the panel colour and the panel gradient underneath it, and opacity and blur act on the picture only. In a tab group the style is painted once for the whole group instead of being covered by each tab.

  • Glass works on tiles under the Minimal clock island

    The cut the island makes into the tile stopped the glass blur from seeing the wallpaper, so those tiles stayed flat. The blur now shows, and the cut stays.

  • The widget shadow is visible

    At any strength it was a thin line along the edge. It now reaches further from the tile as you raise it.

  • Dropdowns close when you tap outside them

    In the Deck key editor, and in any other place where a dropdown sits inside a labelled field, tapping the field's name or the space around the list opened the list again as it closed, and picking an option could leave it open. Tapping outside now closes it.

  • The icon colour of a Deck key works with the Comic key style

    That style always drew the icon in black ink, whatever colour you picked for it. The colour you choose is now used, and keys without one stay in ink.

  • Widgets made by the AI assistant no longer stay blank

    The assistant often wrote a widget's code inside its page, and widgets run only code kept in a file of its own, so the widget installed and then showed an empty tile. Xenon now moves that code into a file before installing the widget or opening it in the Import window.

  • Creations on Sparks no longer stop halfway on Sonnet and Opus

    A whole widget takes these models a minute or more to write, and the connection was cut before the answer arrived, so the assistant said the service was busy and the steps it had already done were charged for nothing. The answer now arrives while it is being written, so long creations finish. When Claude is overloaded for a moment, the assistant waits a few seconds and asks again, twice; a busy answer costs no Sparks. When an answer reaches the length limit in the middle of writing a widget, the assistant asks again once for a shorter version instead of charging for an empty reply. A request to fix a widget no longer ends in "the model did not return an answer": when the quick model starts writing the fix itself, the creation model you chose takes over within seconds.

  • A long creation shows what it is doing, and always arrives

    While the AI assistant works on a creation, the chat says which step it is on (writing, installing and checking, finishing touches) and how long it has been working, and after a while that you can close the chat. If the page reloads or the connection drops in the meantime, the chat picks the answer up when it is ready and the widget still lands on your page; a notice says when it is ready if the chat is closed. If the assistant stops partway, what it had already made stays on your dashboard.

  • Widgets made by the AI assistant fill their tile

    It is now told to size the content from the tile itself, so a countdown or a clock no longer sits small at the bottom of a mostly empty tile.

  • A web page can no longer start a widget install

    Installing a widget package now gets the same protection as installing an icon or sound pack: Xenon refuses the request when it comes from another site or from inside a widget. Installs from the Import dialog and the Store work as before.

  • Full screen no longer shows as a strip

    With the top bar in its minimal style, a tile that goes full screen (Twitch, YouTube, an expanded widget, the Lyrics stage) could appear cut to the width of its own tile, with the rest of the dashboard around it, and fix itself some minutes later. It now covers the whole screen right away.

  • An English song is no longer shown as "Already in your language"

    Now and then the AI provider called a song by its own name for the dashboard language, and Xenon kept that answer for good, so the song had no translation. When the lyrics are clearly in another language, Xenon now tells the AI so, does not accept that answer, and ignores one it had already saved. The song is translated the next time it plays.

  • Lyrics translation works with Sparks only

    If you bought Sparks without a supporter pass, the Lyrics tile asked you to set up Bit even though Bit was ready. It now translates with your Sparks.

  • Running out of Sparks no longer blocks a song

    When the Sparks ran out during a translation, the song was kept as failed for a few minutes, even after you added more. Now the tile says the Sparks ran out and translates again as soon as you have more.

  • Spotify keys on the Deck keep working when Spotify says "rate limited"

    Spotify limits how often an app can talk to it, and an app with a small quota can stay blocked for hours, even when you have not played anything. Play/pause, next and previous keys then failed with the rate-limit error. When Spotify is the app playing on the PC, these three keys now use the Windows media keys instead, which Spotify's limit does not touch, the same way the Spotify tile already did. Keys that need Spotify itself (like, playlists, volume, devices) still wait for the limit to clear. Reported on Discord.

  • A Deck key that mutes the sound shows the right face again

    With a different look while active, the muted face appeared only in the first two minutes after Xenon started, late, and then stopped changing until a restart. The key now follows the mute all the time, also when you mute from the keyboard or from Windows, and changes as soon as you press it. The master volume fader on the Deck follows the same way. Mic mute keys also change at once, instead of a few seconds later. Reported on GitHub.

  • The Xenon app stays on the Edge when you turn the Edge to vertical

    The app remembered the screen it was placed on by its size, 2560 × 720. Rotated, the same screen reports 720 × 2560, so the app took it for a different screen, hid its window and waited for the Edge to come back. A screen turned by 90 degrees is now recognised as the same screen, and the dashboard opens on it in its vertical layout.

  • The "Game detected" suggestion fits a narrow screen

    On a vertical Edge or a phone the message and each button wrapped over three lines in a box half the screen wide. The box now uses the width it needs, and on a narrow screen the buttons sit together on a row under the message.

  • The assistant no longer hears commands nobody gave

    With a silent or muted microphone, Gemini could write a command out of nothing, such as "close everything" or "turn off the kitchen lights", and the assistant then ran it. Xenon now checks that a recording has a voice in it before sending it anywhere, with every assistant, and Gemini is told how to say it heard nobody. When Gemini refuses a recording, the chat now tells you to say it again, instead of acting as if you had not spoken, and the browser microphone now tells Gemini your language, which makes those refusals much rarer. Voice also works when the Gemini model you picked is one Google has closed to new keys, moving to another model as the chat already did, and slow thinking models now get 30 seconds instead of 15 before voice gives up.

  • Web searches no longer fail when the assistant makes two in a row

    Without a Gemini key the assistant searches through DuckDuckGo, which refused a second search made within about 12 seconds, so the assistant could only say it had not managed to check. It now waits for the right moment, so an answer that needs a second search takes a few seconds longer and comes back complete.

  • The assistant works with every Gemini model you can pick

    Xenon asked each Gemini model to skip its thinking step in one fixed way, and Flash-Lite models refuse that request, so with one of them every message failed with "Request contains an invalid argument". Pro models refuse it too, so advanced reasoning quietly answered with the fast model. Xenon now finds the setting each model accepts and remembers it, for chat, voice, web search and the other Gemini features. Three models that cannot run the chat (Nano Banana, Omni, Transcribe) are gone from the model list. When Google says a model is under high demand, the chat now also tries the other models, down to Flash-Lite, before it gives up. Reported on Discord by SWu.

  • The assistant no longer gets stuck on a Gemini model Google has retired

    When Gemini answered that the chosen model is "no longer available", Xenon kept sending the same model and every message failed. It now switches to the newest model your key offers. When a model times out or is overloaded, Xenon waits a little longer (30 seconds) and then tries another model once before showing an error, which names the model that did not answer. Reported on Discord by Rudy.

  • A long song title on a short Media tile fills the space instead of stopping early

    On a short tile the title is limited to one line, but it was cut at the last whole word that fitted, so "BANT CHANT! Legacy Bant..." showed only "BANT CHANT!..." with room to spare, most of all with a larger interface zoom. The title now uses the whole line and ends with an ellipsis where it runs out. Reported on Discord by Piotr.

  • Widgets under the Minimal clock island are cut around it

    A widget that draws its own picture, such as the Haunted House, showed a flat dark strip across its top with the island sitting in it, as if the bar lay on the widget. The picture now runs to the top edge and the island cuts into it, as on the other tiles.

  • A Claude Code session stopped with Esc no longer looks like it is still working

    Pressing Esc in the terminal ends the turn without telling Xenon, so the tile kept showing the spinner and "working" until the next message. Xenon now notices the interruption in the conversation and shows the session as ready within a few seconds.

  • A Claude Code session opens on its latest message

    On a long conversation the whole session panel stretched to the length of the chat, so it opened at the top and you had to scroll to the bottom to see what Claude is writing now. The conversation now scrolls inside its own box and lands on the newest turn.

  • The Claude Code tile scrolls with the mouse wheel again on a session

    When the conversation or the tool log fitted its box, the wheel stopped there and the session never moved, even though the page had more below. The wheel now passes to the session's own scrolling.

  • The Claude Code tile no longer shows a horizontal scrollbar on the Usage page

    A long model cost, such as "1546 USD", was wider than its column and pushed the page sideways at any tile width. The column now grows to fit it.

  • A thermostat no longer turns off when it gets a mode it does not know

    A Home Assistant key or widget that sent a mode Xenon did not recognise switched the climate device off; a media command it did not recognise was sent as play/pause. Both are now refused and the device stays as it was. A mode the device does not offer (for example Heat on an air conditioner that only cools) is refused too.

  • Adding a widget or a page no longer sends you back to the first page

    The dashboard now stays on the page you added the widget to, and a new page opens as soon as you create it.

  • The full top bar no longer piles its buttons over the clock

    On narrow or zoomed screens, and in Layout mode where the page tools take extra room, the buttons drop their labels and keep only their icons before they reach the clock. The labels come back when there is room again.

  • The Volume tab fills its tile again on a vertical screen

    Since 4.11.12, on a display mounted vertically or a phone the Volume tab squeezed into a thin strip and the list of apps was only a few pixels tall, whatever the tile's size. The card and the app list now take their full height again, and the tile scrolls if there are more apps than fit.

  • GPU readings come from your graphics card, not from the processor's built-in graphics

    On a PC with two GPUs and no NVIDIA card, for example a Ryzen 7000 (which has graphics built in) with a Radeon card, VRAM, clock, power and temperature could be read from the built-in graphics while the name showed the card: a Radeon RX 9070 XT appeared with 512 MB of VRAM and 2 W. Xenon now reads every value from the same GPU, the one named on the tile.

  • CPU temperature appears without restarting Xenon once its driver is in place

    If the sensor driver (PawnIO) was installed or updated while Xenon was running, the CPU temperature stayed missing until Xenon was restarted. Now Xenon tries again by itself every 5 minutes. Setup also updates PawnIO when it finds an old version, instead of reporting it as fine: with an old version the CPU temperature could stay missing.

  • Lyrics stay readable in a short Lyrics widget

    The text size followed only the widget's width, so a wide but short widget, especially with the app zoomed to 150% or more, showed lines too big for it and the current line was cut off at the top. The size now follows the height too, so two to three lines always fit.

  • Settings section titles on a phone no longer break into a column of single words

    The short description beside a title now goes under it.

  • The buttons in the Store's Installed tab stay inside their row on a phone

    On a narrow screen, Add to page, Suspend and Remove ran past the left edge of the row. They now wrap and share the width.

  • Add to page works for a widget folder you just added

    A widget copied into the widgets folder while the dashboard was open showed up in the Store's Installed tab, but its Add to page button did nothing until you reloaded the page. It now picks up the new widget and adds it, and says so if it still cannot.

  • The Layout button's icon is visible again while Layout mode is on

    It was drawn dark on a dark button.

  • Windows setup no longer stops halfway when your user name has a dot in it

    On some PCs (for example a user named "Mr.Name") the app's "Complete setup" stopped with "An object at the specified path ... does not exist", and every retry stopped at the same point. Xenon itself opened, but CPU temperature, fan speeds and in-game FPS never got set up. Setup now gets past it, including on a PC where an earlier attempt already failed.

  • Start-up work ran twice with paired devices on

    With paired access on, Xenon repeated its start-up jobs at every boot. It now runs them once.

  • Remote Control finds Sunshine without winget

    A Sunshine whose service is on the PC now counts as installed, even if winget does not know it.

  • Coming back to the dashboard no longer leaves it working for nothing

    If a tile redrew itself while the screen was idle, the animation on its old copy started again at your next touch, on something no longer on screen, and kept the dashboard busy at the full speed of your monitor until the page reloaded. In our test on a 240 Hz screen one of these doubled the CPU the page used. A tile redrawing through a long idle also no longer holds its old copies in memory.

  • Song lyrics hold still in Performance Mode

    With animations paused, lyrics kept gliding and lighting up word by word. They now hold still, as they do in a game.

  • Performance Mode no longer adds a power plan each time

    With Ultimate Performance chosen, every session left one more copy in the list of Windows power plans. It now keeps to one, and a plan that was already on stays on when the session ends.

  • An app that refuses a priority change is not a failed session

    Anti-cheat and apps running as administrator can refuse the boost. The session now says it is on, instead of showing an error.

  • The Performance Mode window shows only what applies

    The priority switch showed even with no app to boost, and ticking it did nothing. It now appears only when there is an app to boost.

4.11.13 16 October 2026

Added

  • A Deck key can now change the dashboard page

    The new action "Go to page" (in the System group) turns the dashboard to one of your pages, picked from a list of your own pages, or to the next page, the previous one, or back to the page you were on. Put it on a key, in a Multi-Action after other steps, or on a double tap or hold. It turns the screen the key was pressed on; from the Virtual Deck window it turns the dashboards on this PC. The Xenon AI can also add it when it builds a Deck for you. Asked on Discord by SeibiRiho.

  • Widgets can now show Home Assistant history and cameras

    A widget with the Home Assistant permission can ask for the last hours (up to 3 days) of the devices you picked in Settings → Home Assistant, to draw a temperature or power trace, and for a frame from one of your cameras. It only ever gets the devices you picked; anything else is refused without Home Assistant being asked. Weather entities now come with temperature, humidity and wind, and a person's entry says whether they are home or in which zone, never where they are on a map. Every device also says when its state last changed, so a widget can show how long a door has been open. Widgets also learn which copy of the tile they are in, so two copies of one widget can show two different rooms. The SDK guide is updated.

  • Home Assistant keys and widgets can set exact values

    Four new choices on the Deck's Home Assistant actions, also open to widgets: a thermostat's temperature, a light's colour temperature in kelvin, a media player's volume, and how far a cover or blind is open. Type the number in the key's Value field. An empty value does nothing, it never turns a device off.

  • Widget Deck macros can change page too

    A widget package that declares the pages permission can use the same action in its Deck macros, which turns every dashboard watching, like a page shortcut. The SDK guide is updated.

  • Song lyrics for whatever is playing

    A new lyrics button next to the playback controls of the Media tile shows the lyrics of the current song over the blurred cover, with the line being sung highlighted and the text scrolling in time. Inside that line the words light up one by one, karaoke style; LRCLIB times whole lines, so the pace of the words is an estimate from their syllables. To keep the lines on time, Xenon (and the Xenon Helper) now reads where the song is to the millisecond instead of in whole seconds; widgets that listen to the media stream get it as positionMs (documented in the SDK guide). When a lyrics file marks no instrumental break, the pause dots appear once the line has surely been sung, instead of the last line staying lit through the break. Play, pause, the seek bar, the Spotify buttons and the volume stay on screen while the lyrics are open. It works with any player Xenon sees: Spotify, YouTube in the browser, Apple Music, VLC and the others, on Windows, macOS and Linux. Tap a line to jump there in the song, or drag the lyrics to look ahead; they follow the song again after a few seconds. Songs with plain lyrics show them as a list, and live streams say that there is no timing to follow. The lyrics come from LRCLIB, a free lyrics library: Xenon sends it the title, artist and length of the song, nothing else. To turn it off, use Settings → Appearance → Song lyrics.

  • Lyrics widget for supporters

    A tile just for the lyrics, in large type you can read from across the room, over the blurred cover of the song. It unlocks with your supporter pass, like Developer cleanup. Before that you can try it free for 7 days, with every feature and no code: once per PC, from the button on the locked tile, which then shows the date the trial ends. The widget list now says in one line what it adds:

    • Timing per song. If one song's lyrics run ahead or behind, fix it with − and +. The fix is kept for that song only and comes back the next time it plays. Tap the value to drop it. A timing for every song (for a player that is always late) is in the widget's options.
    • Translation under each line, in the dashboard language, through the AI provider you set up in Xenon AI. It is off until you turn it on, and the options say plainly what it costs: one request per new song, sent only after 20 seconds of listening, so skipping through a playlist costs nothing. Songs already translated are kept and never paid for again. A monthly limit (50, 200 or 500 songs) and a counter of songs and tokens keep the bill in view. The options also show what 100 new songs cost on your provider, worked out from your own translations and the provider's published prices, with the date of those prices and a link to them. The prices are kept up to date from the Xenon site, so a price change reaches you without an update. With Ollama it is free and stays on your PC. With Gemini, OpenAI or Anthropic, translation uses the provider's small low-cost model (Flash-Lite, mini or Haiku), even if you picked a bigger one for the assistant. With Claude Code or Codex there is nothing to pay per song, but each new song counts toward your Claude or ChatGPT plan's usage limits, like a message you send; the options say so before you turn it on and show how many tokens a song has used so far. These run on the plan's small model too (Haiku on Claude Code).
    • Reading for Japanese, Korean and Chinese: the line in Latin letters, in the same request as the translation.
    • Stage mode (a switch in the options): when music starts, the tile fills the screen, and it gives the dashboard back 8 seconds after the music stops, with ✕ or with Esc. There is also a button to do it by hand.
  • A Deck key that opens an app can now pass it arguments

    The "Open app" action has a new optional field, Arguments, for things like --restore-last-session (Edge brings back the tabs of the last session) or --profile-directory="Profile 1". Type them as you would after the program name in a terminal; put quotes around anything with a space in it. On Windows they apply to an .exe (a .lnk shortcut already carries its own, so the key says so instead of starting the app and ignoring them), on Linux to a program or AppImage (not to a .desktop entry), and on a Mac they are used when the app starts, so an app that is already open ignores them. Asked on GitHub by wadejtopp-pixel.

  • Messages from the Claude tile now arrive in the open Claude Code session

    When a session is open and waiting for you, a message you write for it on the Claude tile shows up in that session as if you had typed it there, and Claude answers there, so the terminal and the tile show the same conversation. Before, the tile continued the session in a separate run in the background, and the open terminal never saw it. The box says where the message is going before you send it, and if Claude Code does not take it, the message comes back into the box with the reason. Commands that start with / still have to be typed in the session itself. This needs the Xenon mod for Claude Code 0.3.0: run claude plugin update xenon@xenon and start a new session. To go back to the background run, turn off "Messages from the Xenon tile" in the mod's options. Without the mod, the tile works as before.

Improvements

  • Supporting Xenon monthly is now one tap away

    Settings → Support Xenon offers a monthly membership next to the one-time coffee, and the Store's "Become a supporter" buttons open the membership page directly. These links pass through the Xenon supporter server, which counts how many times each button is pressed (a daily total per button, nothing about you) and then opens Buy Me a Coffee.

  • How many people support Xenon, and how many it takes

    Settings → Support Xenon now shows how many people support Xenon right now and how many it takes for Xenon to cover its own costs, with a bar. Once that number is reached, the bar goes away and the line says thank you instead, and that anything beyond it becomes time to make Xenon better. In December, a short note from the maker of Xenon may appear once in the corner, with the same count. It shows only if you have used Xenon for at least a month, at least a month after the one-time supporter card, and never during a game, a voice chat, an Ambient scene or the lock screen. Closing it, or pressing either support button, hides it until next December; "I already support Xenon" hides it for good. The two numbers come from the Xenon supporter server, and Xenon sends nothing to get them: the request is the same from every PC.

  • Xenon uses less CPU while it sits on screen

    Asked on Reddit. What changed, with nothing to set up:

    • GPU usage on AMD and Intel graphics. On PCs without an NVIDIA card, Xenon read GPU usage in a way that took 5 to 13 seconds per reading on our test PC, longer than the 5 seconds between readings, so the sensor reader never rested. It now reads the same figure in a fraction of a second. The disk activity reading also stopped starting a new PowerShell every time.
    • NVIDIA fans and Corsair PSUs. With LibreHardwareMonitor installed, each reading of the graphics card's fan speeds refreshed every sensor of the card, and each reading of a Corsair i-series PSU asked it for every value it reports (voltages, currents, temperatures, uptime). Xenon now asks only for the fan speeds and for the watts and fan it shows. On our test PC the two readings now take less than half as long, with the same numbers.
    • Widgets that list running apps (the processes stream). Building the list every 2 seconds now takes about 45 ms of CPU instead of about 110 ms on our test PC, with the same list.
    • Battery. The battery is checked only when a battery tile, a widget or a Deck key shows it.
    • The lock screen and the Ambient canvas scenes update their clock once a second instead of checking it on every frame of the display (up to 240 times a second).
    • Animations that start while the dashboard is idle now pause like the others, instead of running until the next touch.
    • Animated backgrounds made with code wake the page only when they draw a frame, and hold still behind Settings and other frosted panels, like the built-in background already did.
    • Video wallpapers pause while a game is in front and in Performance mode, and start again by themselves. A paused video keeps its picture.
    • The Media tile's waveform draws at most 60 frames a second and stops in Game mode, Performance mode and behind frosted panels. The microphone tile's rotating ring stops in Game mode and Performance mode.
    • File search (Xenon Helper) builds and updates its index in Windows' efficiency mode, so it no longer competes with a game or your own work for a fast CPU core. Searches still run at full speed.

Fixed

  • macOS: the Network card shows your download and upload speed again

    On some Macs it always read 0, because the system command Xenon asks for the traffic counters also looked up a name for every network address, and that took longer than Xenon waits. It now skips the name lookups, which also saves a few network requests every 3 seconds. Reported on GitHub by trippo, who also found the fix. Widgets that graph one network link on its own also read the right numbers for VPN tunnels now, which have one column fewer in that output.

  • Lyrics translation no longer says "already in your language" on a song in another language

    The AI now names the language the lyrics are sung in and Xenon compares it with yours, instead of trusting a yes or no that could be wrong.

  • Codex approvals: a note about automatic approval

    If Codex has automatic approval turned on, it can approve a command before you answer on the Xenon screen. The Codex setting now says so.

  • On a PC with two graphics chips, Xenon now renders on the one that drives the screen you chose

    It used to pick the Xeneon Edge, or else the main screen, even when you had chosen another screen in Settings → Display. If that screen was on the other chip, every frame was copied between the two, which costs CPU and GPU all the time. Applies to the Xenon app on Windows.

  • A video wallpaper no longer starts again behind Settings when you tap inside it

    It is meant to hold still while Settings is open, but any tap restarted it.

  • Claude's questions on the tile are easier to read

    When the choices of a question have a description, they now stack one under the other, like in the terminal, instead of sitting side by side with the text cut off. The Other row says that you can type your own answer.

  • The Claude tile shows a reply once, not twice

    When the tile continued a session in the background, the reply appeared in the conversation and again in a card under it. It now appears once, in the conversation. If the session is still open in a terminal without the Xenon mod 0.3.0, the box also says before you send that the reply will come in the tile and not in the terminal.

  • The Claude tile now says how long the current answer has been going

    It counted from when the session was opened, so in a session open for an hour it showed "1h" a second after you sent a message.

  • Files attached to a message for a working Claude session now go with it

    While a session was busy, a message you wrote for it on the tile was delivered without the files you had attached. The files now go with the message, as they already did for a new task.

  • The Xenon chat now really sends your pictures to Claude Code and Codex

    With either of those as the AI, an image you attached or pasted never reached the model: it answered that it could not see anything. The picture of the message you send is now passed to the program (up to 4 PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP images, 10 MB each), so "explain this card" or "what is in this screenshot" works. Pictures from earlier messages are still only mentioned, not re-sent. Tested with Claude Code; the Codex path could not be run here.

  • Events with a start and an end time now stay in Upcoming until they end

    A 5 p.m. to 11 p.m. event used to drop off the Upcoming list (and the lock screen) soon after 5 p.m., because only its start time was checked. It now stays until its end time, like an all-day event stays all day. Events with no end time behave as before. Reported on Discord by Piotr.

  • Widgets added while the interface is scaled now fit their tile in the macOS app

    The 4.11.12 fix covered widgets already on the dashboard when the scale changed, but a Store widget such as Nocturne Now Playing added while the scale was already above 100% still came out enlarged and cropped until the scale was changed and set back. The macOS app now applies the scale again whenever a widget loads. Reported on Discord by Piotr.

  • Codex hooks now start on Windows

    On some Codex versions (the ChatGPT app included) every Xenon hook failed with "hook exited with code 1", so the Codex tile never saw the session and approvals never reached Xenon. Codex cannot run a command that contains quotes, and Xenon's did, because Node lives in Program Files. Xenon now writes a small codex-hook.cmd in its data folder and points the hooks at it (if your Windows user name has a space in it, this is not done yet and the hooks stay as they were). After updating, open /hooks in Codex once and trust the hooks again, as Codex asks whenever a hook command changes. Reported on Discord by The.GothamKnight.

  • On a Mac, Update now updates the Xenon app too, not only the dashboard

    The Xenon app has two parts: the app you open, and the dashboard inside it. On a Mac, updating restarted the whole app once the dashboard was done, and the app part was never reached, so the app stayed on an older version. Fixes that live in the app, like bringing the window back to its screen after sleep, never arrived, and Settings still said you were up to date. Xenon now finishes the app part when it starts again after the update. When the two parts are on different versions, Settings shows both, and Update available stays on until the app has caught up. The crash log now also notes when the app updates itself and why an update failed. Reported on Discord by Piotr.

  • On Windows, the Xenon app now keeps up with the dashboard when automatic updates are on

    Automatic updates only ever updated the dashboard; the app waited for you to tap its update message. Now, once the dashboard is on the new version, the app follows at a moment when you are not using the PC, like the dashboard does. A failed try is not repeated on its own, and the Update button still works. On a Mac and on Linux the app still waits for your tap, because there the system can ask for your password.

4.11.12 9 October 2026

Added

  • See and delete your Claude Code chats from the Claude tile

    A new Chats tab lists every chat Claude Code keeps on this PC, newest first, with its project, when it was last used and how much space it takes (sub-agents and file checkpoints included). Tap a chat to read or continue it; tick the ones you no longer need and they go to the Recycle Bin/Trash after a confirmation, so you can still restore them. A chat that is open or was written in the last few minutes is never moved.

  • The Claude tile is redesigned to look and work like Claude Code

    Your sessions are now a list on the left and the one you pick is open beside it, so you always know which chat you are reading and writing to. Each session has its own colour and its own Clawd, Claude Code's mascot, which walks while it works, hops when it needs you, blinks when it is done and sleeps once it has ended. A session is named the way Claude Code names it (your /rename, or its own summary), with the project, branch and the first characters of its id under it, instead of three rows all reading "xenon". The open session reads like the terminal: a status line with the ✻ spinner and what Claude is doing, its model, permission mode, effort, context and cost, the plan as Claude Code's checklist, the last tool calls, the conversation, and a prompt box with "> ". A request from the session you are reading appears inside it; one from another session is a single line on top that takes you there. The 5-hour and weekly limits sit in the header, with the full details under Usage. On a narrow tile or a phone the list becomes a row of chips above the session. With nothing running, Clawd waits with the prompt to start a new session. A new session can start in plan mode, with edits accepted, or asking for everything, and with the effort you pick, the same options as the terminal; only what your Claude Code supports is offered, and never a mode that skips permissions. Type "/" to pick one of your commands or skills, with arrows and Enter. A session started from the tile now shows what it is doing and its last tool calls while it runs.

  • Tiles can be resized from the top-left corner too

    In layout editing every tile now has a second resize handle at its top-left, just under its toolbar, next to the one at the bottom-right. To fill free space above or to the left of a tile, drag that handle instead of moving the tile first and then resizing it.

  • File search answers while you type, and finds more of what you mean

    Results come from Xenon's index straight away, and what Windows Search adds (including files that only match inside their content) follows below a line, without moving the rows already on screen. While you keep typing a word, each letter only re-checks the previous matches: on a 2.5 million file C: drive a query went from 52 to 118 ms down to 19 to 54 ms, measured against the previous build. Folders are results too, in their own group, and words can match the folders above a file, so "download fattura" finds the invoice in Download. A file you opened from Xenon before is never pushed out of the list, and is found even with a small typo, like an app name ("spotfy"). Apps you launch from the search come first among equal matches. Searching inside documents now matches words as you type them ("fatt" finds "fattura"), as file names already did.

  • The search is easier to read and to drive

    Results are grouped (Apps, Folders, Files, In the content). The empty search shows the files and folders you opened recently from Xenon; in the Search widget this is off unless you turn it on in Settings → Search and disk, because a paired phone sees that tile too. A Filters button adds type, date and size without typing them, as the same chips you can remove. In the search popup, an image result shows a preview beside the list. Ctrl+Enter shows the selected result in its folder and Ctrl+C copies its path.

  • Search on macOS and Linux finds your apps, and on a Mac it searches inside files

    Off Windows the Applications group was always empty. It now lists the .app bundles on a Mac and the installed applications on Linux (the same entries your app menu shows). On a Mac the search also asks Spotlight, the way it asks Windows Search on a PC, so it finds files outside Xenon's index and words inside documents. Both are new on those platforms and still in beta, like the macOS and Linux versions themselves.

  • The Disk tile tells you what changed, not only what is big

    The overview is now a bar of the whole drive split by kind (video, photos, music, documents, archives, apps, games, other files, the part Xenon cannot index, and free space), with a legend, and below it up to three lines worth reading: how much you can free right now, which folder grew the most in the last week ("The Download\Video folder grew by 11 GB in 7 days"), and, once there are a few weeks of history, when the drive fills up at the current rate or that it is stable. Anything in a Steam, Epic, Xbox, GOG, Riot, EA or Rockstar games folder counts as a game, whatever its extension. Xenon keeps one small reading per drive per day for 90 days to know this; it stays on your PC. Tapping the growth line opens that folder in the map. Explore has a new list of large files nobody has modified for over a year. The map has the path above it, so you can tap back to any level instead of one step at a time, and a file in the map, in the lists or among the duplicates has a button that shows it selected in its folder (on the PC; not from a paired phone, where it would open a window nobody sees). On a wide tile like the Xeneon Edge the bar and the lines sit beside the map.

  • The Disk tile opens at once and never goes blank

    On a big drive the tile showed "Aggregating millions of files" for up to half a minute, every time you switched drive or tapped refresh: we measured 26.7 seconds on a 2.5 million file C: drive, almost all of it spent re-reading up to 2 GB of files to confirm duplicates. Duplicates are now confirmed in the background, starting from the first and last 64 KB of each file and remembering the result for files that have not changed, so the next analysis does not read them again. The tile answers with what is already confirmed and the list fills in by itself. That also removed the old 200 MB limit, which hid the duplicates most worth finding (ISOs, videos, game archives). A drive you return to is redrawn immediately and refreshed in place, an analysis is reused for as long as nothing on the drive changed, and after a restart the tile shows the last analysis with its age while the index is being rebuilt.

  • A Deck key can switch to the first output that is connected

    Pick up to three outputs in order: First choice, If it is not connected, Then (optional). When you press the key, Xenon looks at what is plugged in at that moment and sends the sound to the first one on the list that is there: your headphones when they are on, the speakers when they are not. It works the same for a dock's DAC and the laptop speakers, or a TV and a monitor. If the first available output is already the one in use, nothing is switched, so the sound does not drop out for nothing. If none of them is connected, the key says so. Its face lights up while the first choice is the output in use. Widgets can do it too, with { type: 'audioDeviceFirst', device1, device2, device3 } under the existing audioDevice permission, so it asks for nothing new (WIDGET_SDK.md, section 5g). Asked on Discord for a key that closes a set of apps and then goes to "my Bluetooth headphones if they are connected, otherwise the speakers": until now that took two steps, passed through the speakers first and flashed red whenever the headphones were off.

  • The "+" panel says where a widget is when it is already on your dashboard

    The panel only offers widgets that are not placed yet, so one you had added, Weather for instance, was simply missing from the list, and that reads as a widget that vanished. They are now listed too, under Already on your dashboard: the same items, quieter, each saying where it is (this page, another page by name, or a tab of this tile), and a tap takes you there, turning to the page and lighting the tile for a moment. The search finds them as well, so typing "weather" lands on it instead of on an empty list. If a widget is marked as placed but no tile is on any page, the tap puts it on the page you are on. Asked on Discord: "where is the Weather widget in my menu, it disappeared".

  • A native package for Arch Linux and Omarchy (#133)

    On Arch Linux and the distributions built on it, npm run native:build:arch builds the Xenon app and packages it for pacman, so it installs, shows up in the app menu and uninstalls like any other package (sudo pacman -U). It is built on your own PC rather than downloaded, since the release builds run on Ubuntu. Because pacman owns the installed app, Xenon does not try to replace it; the dashboard still updates itself as usual. (Thanks to the community contribution behind this.)

  • New ways to watch in the Twitch and YouTube tiles

    Under the video there are now three buttons. Cinema shows the video and the Twitch chat side by side, or for YouTube the video and your list, without the rest of the tile. Fill the tile gives the whole tile to the video, with the controls over the picture. Full screen now keeps the chat (or the list) next to the video, and a button switches it off when you want only the picture. The tile remembers the view you picked on each screen, so the Xeneon Edge and your phone can use different ones. Tap the same button again to go back to the normal tile; Esc or changing page leaves full screen.

  • Choose which Twitch account the player in the Twitch tile uses, or watch anonymously

    The video in the tile is Twitch's own player, and it only knows you if you are signed in to twitch.tv in the browser that shows the dashboard. The account you connect in Settings → Streaming is what fills the lists, and the player cannot see it. In the Xenon app the player had never been signed in, so on the Xeneon Edge every stream played as a guest, even when your followed channels were on screen. A new account button under the video now says how the player is watching ("Signed in as …", or not signed in) and offers two choices: With my Twitch account or Anonymously. In the Xenon app on Windows, Sign in to Twitch opens Twitch's own sign-in page in a window on your main screen. You type your password into Twitch, not into Xenon. When you are done the window closes and the player starts again signed in, so a subscription or Twitch Turbo applies in the tile as it does on twitch.tv. Anonymously plays without your account but keeps your sign-in, so you can switch back at any time. In a browser, sign in on twitch.tv as usual; on an iPhone or iPad the player always watches anonymously. Ads that a streamer starts during the live go to every viewer who is not subscribed, signed in or not.

  • The Twitch and YouTube tiles are rearranged so they have no empty space

    The video is now as large as the tile allows and the name and the controls sit right under it, instead of the video floating in a taller box with empty bands above and below. On a wide, short tile like the Xeneon Edge the video takes the full height with the list and the chat beside it; on a box-shaped tile with the Twitch chat on, the list goes under the video and the chat takes the full height on the right. When nothing is playing the tile shows only the list, which spreads over several columns on a wide tile, instead of a black box asking you to pick something. The channel or video that is playing is marked in the list, the tabs are plain words, and the chat has a header with the button that opens the full Twitch chat.

  • A Codex tile for OpenAI Codex

    Add Codex from the "+" panel and it shows the usage windows of your plan, read from Codex itself (5 hours and a week on a paid plan, one 30-day window on Free), with the time to each reset and a marker for an even pace, plus your tokens per day for the last 30 days and the conversations Codex lists, the most recently active first. Tap one to read it: the open conversation keeps itself up to date, and while Codex is still working it also shows Codex's progress notes, which give way to the final answer when the turn ends. It covers Codex wherever you use it: the ChatGPT desktop app, the Codex extension for your editor and the codex command. Tap Codex → Connect and Xenon adds five small hooks to your Codex hooks.json (your own hooks stay as they are and a copy of the file is kept); after you trust them once in Codex with /hooks, the tile shows the sessions that are working and you can answer their requests on this screen: Allow, Deny, or Answer in Codex, which puts the question back in Codex at once. Each request says what it would do (the command, or the files a change touches, with deletes marked) and what makes it unusual, and a request that cannot be undone is allowed by holding the key. While a request waits here Codex does not show its own, so it goes back to Codex after 90 seconds (Settings → Codex changes this, or turns the requests off). Xenon never trusts the hooks for you: that step is Codex's own safety check and stays yours. Widgets can read the plan numbers through the new codex stream, which carries numbers only, never a folder, a project, a conversation or a command (WIDGET_SDK.md, section 3h).

  • An Ask ChatGPT tile

    Add Ask ChatGPT from the "+" panel and type a question: the answer comes from your own ChatGPT plan, through OpenAI's Codex on this PC, with no API key. ChatGPT itself has no way for another app to read or continue your chats, so this is the route OpenAI allows: the answers do not appear in your ChatGPT history and are kept on this PC instead, up to 40 conversations. While an answer is being written the tile shows how long it has been thinking, with Stop; a follow-up carries the conversation so far. Chats lists your conversations, lets you delete them and pick the model, and the header shows how much of your plan's busiest usage window is used, since these answers count against it. It needs Codex installed and signed in (the ChatGPT app, the editor extension or the codex command), and says so when it is not.

  • CPU and GPU temperatures can use their own unit

    In Settings → Weather, below Temperature unit, Hardware temperatures can be set to °C or °F on its own, so the forecast can be in °F while the CPU and GPU, the Guardian alerts and the game session recap stay in °C (or the other way round). It starts on Same as weather, so nothing changes unless you pick a unit. Installed widgets are told the hardware unit too (hwTempUnit).

  • A Xenon mod for Claude Code

    Claude Code can now load mods, and Xenon has one. Pressing Connect Claude Code on the Claude tile now also asks Claude Code to install it, and starts with the next Claude Code session. A Claude Code connected earlier gets an Install the mod button on the tile, and the install can also be typed by hand: /plugin install xenon --marketplace marcimastro98/Xenon. Disconnect removes it. It needs a Claude Code that supports mods. The tile then shows which model each subagent runs on, and the context gauge and the 5-hour and weekly limits update as soon as they change instead of waiting for the next status line. In Claude Code, /xenon says whether the dashboard hears that session, without using any tokens. The mod finds Xenon through the connection the Claude tile already made, so there is nothing to pair. It sends numbers and model names only: never what you type, what Claude runs or the content of your files. When Xenon is closed the mod waits and tries again later, without slowing Claude Code down. Under the Claude Code prompt, a line appears only when something needs you: Xenon is closed or not linked, or an approval is waiting on the dashboard. While all is well there is no line; /xenon gives the detail. The line can be turned off in the mod's options. Also in the options, off by default: Approve from the Xenon dashboard. Permission requests then appear on the dashboard for a short wait you choose (30 seconds unless you change it); with no answer there, the terminal asks as usual. Only a tap on the card approves, and the card gets the command, file path or address, never the content. The existing connection keeps working with or without it.

  • A Developer cleanup tile, for supporters

    On a PC used for development most of the full disk is not in your files: it is Docker images and build cache, local AI models in Ollama, VS Code and Cursor folders for projects you deleted long ago, and the virtual disks of WSL and Docker, which grow and never shrink by themselves. The Disk tile cannot see any of that. Add Developer cleanup from the "+" panel and it shows how much each one takes and how much you can free. Docker removes images no container uses and the build cache, with Docker's own commands (images in use and your volumes are not touched). Ollama lists your models to pick from; the one Xenon's AI uses is kept. Editor folders lists only the folders of projects that no longer exist on disk, and moves them to the Recycle Bin or Trash. On Windows, a WSL or Docker virtual disk of 10 GB or more gets a Compact button: Windows asks for administrator permission, Xenon closes Docker and WSL and shrinks the file. Each step says what happens before it runs. A source that is not installed or not running says so instead of showing zero. The tile is unlocked with your supporter code, typed right in the tile or already saved in Settings, and stays unlocked on that PC for good; without a code it says so and offers a way to become a supporter. The space numbers, with no names, are also open to any widget through the new devStorage stream (WIDGET_SDK.md); the cleanup itself is not, so a widget can never delete anything. The "+" panel marks it "For supporters", so you know before adding it. If Docker or Ollama is off, the tile checks again every 30 seconds while it is on screen, so starting them shows up without a refresh.

Fixed

  • The Claude tile always shows the end of a reply

    With a session open in the tile, the terminal could finish its turn while the tile kept showing the conversation without the final answer. The tile read the conversation once when the turn ended, sometimes a moment before Claude Code had written the last message, and never looked again; a session that went from waiting on you to finished was not re-read at all, and an answer arriving late could overwrite a newer one. The tile now reads again a few times after every change until Claude Code has closed the turn, shows the final reply as soon as Claude Code reports it, never cuts the newest message short (older long ones have Show all), and offers a New reply button when you have scrolled up instead of jumping. A request left over from earlier in the turn no longer keeps the session marked as waiting after it has finished.

  • In the Discord widget's Controls tab, the volume rows now sit below the people in your call

    The microphone and speaker volume used to sit between the buttons and the list of people, pushing the people down. The order is now the buttons, the people in the call, then the two volumes and the audio options.

  • The Linux app no longer closes by itself a few seconds after opening

    4.11.11 moved Xenon's own screen checks onto the thread that draws the window, but the app could still quit with an "[xcb] Unknown sequence number" error, because something else in the app, such as the tray icon, could still talk to the display server from another thread at the same moment. Xenon now tells the display library at startup that it is used from several threads, so those moments wait their turn instead of ending the app.

  • The Minimal bar's island fits the music again

    The floating island could never be wider than half the screen, so with the clock, date, weather and a song in it the title disappeared and the music controls ran into the page dots or past the island's edge. The island now takes the room its content needs, up to the width of the screen, and shortens the title only when the screen is really too narrow.

  • Deck folder keys bring the folder to the front

    On Windows, a key that opens a folder opened it behind the other windows, or minimized, because Windows does not let File Explorer take the foreground on its own. Xenon now finds the folder's window and brings it forward, as app keys already did.

  • Codex no longer reports an issue with Xenon's hooks

    Codex's hooks list showed "1 issue loading hooks", because Xenon marked its session-end hook to run in the background, which Codex does not allow for that event. The hook now runs the way Codex expects. Xenon updates it by itself the next time it starts; Codex may then ask you to trust the hooks again.

  • The Codex tile shows the same plan limits as Codex

    Codex also reports extra limits, such as one named "gpt-reserve", that its own usage menu does not show, and the tile listed them as a third row nobody could place. The tile now shows the main 5-hour and weekly limits, and an extra one only when it is the limit that is stopping you.

  • Widgets keep their size in the macOS app when the interface is scaled

    With the interface scale above 100%, the macOS app enlarged the inside of Store widgets such as Nocturne Now Playing without giving them more room, so their text looked blurry and their bottom controls were cut off behind scroll bars. The macOS app now scales the page the way Safari zoom does, so widgets stay sharp and fit their tile, as they already did in a browser and on Windows.

  • The top bar keeps the same height from one song to the next

    The now-playing part of the bar took the width of each track title, so a long title squeezed the Lock, Ambient, Xenon and Search buttons into two rows and a short one let them back into one, making the whole bar change height with the music. The track text now has a fixed width in the full bar, so the layout only changes when playback starts or stops.

  • Downloading Whisper works again

    Since September the whisper.cpp project no longer attaches its Windows files to its numbered versions, so Download Whisper (Settings → Xenon AI, and the "Hey Xenon" row) found nothing and stopped at once.
